examples.text:
Title: Academic Course Timetabling
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter
Description: Assign university courses to classrooms and time slots. Courses can only be assigned to eligible rooms (meeting capacity requirements). No room can host two courses simultaneously. Maximize total faculty slot preference.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total slot preference score across all scheduled course-room-slot assignments
Decision variables: schedule[c,r,sl]: 1 if course c is scheduled in room r at slot sl (binary, only for eligible course-room pairs)
Parameters: eligibility[c,r]: 1 if course c can use room r (sparse); slot_preference[c,sl]: faculty preference for course c in slot sl
Constraint: Each course is scheduled in exactly one room-slot combination
Constraint: Each room-slot combination hosts at most one course

Title: Clinic Appointment Scheduling
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter
Description: A clinic schedules patient appointments to time slots and clinicians. Each patient must be seen exactly once by a clinician they are eligible for (sparse). Each clinician can handle at most one patient per slot. Maximize total patient preference score.

Parameters: eligible[Patients, Clinicians]: 1 if patient p is eligible to see clinician cl (sparse); pref[Patients, Slots]: patient preference score for each slot

Constraint: Each clinician handles at most one patient per slot

examples.name: assignment

Title: Worker-Task Assignment Problem
Keywords: binary variable
Description: A project manager must assign a set of workers to a set of tasks for an upcoming project. The number of workers equals the number of tasks. Each worker must be assigned to exactly one task, and each task must be handled by exactly one worker. The cost of assigning a particular worker to a particular task is known (reflecting skill fit, training requirements, or opportunity cost). Find the one-to-one assignment of workers to tasks that minimizes total assignment cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total assignment cost summed over all worker-task pairs that are assigned
Decision variables: assign[w,t]: 1 if worker w is assigned to task t, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: assignment_cost[w,t]: cost of assigning worker w to task t
Constraint: Each worker must be assigned to exactly one task
Constraint: Each task must be assigned exactly one worker

examples.name: assignment_nurse_rostering
examples.text:
Title: Weekly Nurse Rostering
Keywords: binary variable
Description: A hospital must create a weekly schedule for five nurses across three shifts (morning, afternoon, night) and seven days. Each shift on each day has a minimum number of nurses required to provide adequate patient care. Each nurse has a shift-specific cost (reflecting overtime, seniority, and preference). No nurse may work more than a specified maximum number of shifts per week. Determine the minimum-cost weekly schedule that meets all coverage requirements without exceeding nurse working-hour limits.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total scheduling cost across all nurse-shift-day assignments
Decision variables: assign[n,s,d]: 1 if nurse n is assigned to shift s on day d, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: shift_cost[n,s]: cost of scheduling nurse n for shift s (per occurrence); min_nurses[s,d]: minimum number of nurses required for shift s on day d; max_weekly_shifts[n]: maximum number of shifts nurse n can work per week
Constraint: For each shift on each day, the number of nurses assigned must meet or exceed the minimum required coverage
Constraint: For each nurse, the total number of shift assignments across the week must not exceed their maximum allowed weekly shifts

No nurse may work more than a specified maximum number of shifts per week. Determine the minimum-cost weekly schedule that meets all coverage requirements without exceeding nurse working-hour limits.

assign.description: 1 if nurse n is assigned to shift s on day d, 0 otherwise
assign.label: nurse_assignments

examples.name: assignment_operator_job_period
examples.text:
Title: Operator-Job-Period Assignment with Eligibility
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter, sparse filter
Description: A production facility must assign six operators to eight jobs across four shifts. Operators are qualified for only certain jobs (based on their certifications and training), defining eligible (operator, job) pairs. Each (job, shift) pair that requires coverage must have exactly one operator assigned to it. An operator can handle at most a maximum number of jobs per shift. Each eligible (operator, job) pair has a known cost per shift. Minimize total assignment cost while covering all required job-shift slots and respecting operator qualifications and workload limits.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost of operator-job-period assignments
Decision variables: assign[o,j,p]: 1 if operator o is assigned to job j in period p (only for eligible operator-job pairs), 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: cost_per_shift[o,j]: cost per shift of assigning operator o to job j (only defined for eligible pairs); job_required[j,p]: 1 if job j needs coverage in period p, 0 otherwise; max_jobs_per_shift[o]: maximum number of jobs operator o can handle in any single shift
Constraint: For each (job, shift) pair that requires coverage, exactly one eligible operator must be assigned
Constraint: For each operator in each shift, the total number of jobs assigned must not exceed their maximum jobs per shift

Title: Skill-Based Worker-Task Assignment
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter
Description: A project manager must assign eight workers to ten tasks. Workers have different skill sets, so only certain worker-task combinations are eligible (a worker can only perform tasks they are qualified for). Each eligible assignment has a known cost reflecting training requirements, efficiency, and worker preference. Each task must be assigned to exactly one eligible worker. Each worker may handle at most a maximum number of tasks. Find the minimum-cost assignment of workers to tasks that covers all tasks while respecting eligibility and workload constraints.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total assignment cost across all worker-task pairs assigned
Decision variables: assign[w,t]: 1 if worker w is assigned to task t (only for eligible pairs), 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: assignment_cost[w,t]: cost of assigning worker w to task t (only defined for eligible pairs); max_tasks[w]: maximum number of tasks that worker w can handle
Constraint: Each task must be assigned to exactly one eligible worker
Constraint: Each worker may be assigned to at most their maximum allowed number of tasks

examples.name: assignment_team_project
examples.text:
Title: Team-to-Project Assignment for Maximum Value
Keywords: binary variable
Description: A consulting firm has four teams and six client projects. Each project must be assigned to at least one team (a project can be handled by multiple teams if needed). Each team can take on at most a maximum number of projects simultaneously. Different teams have different expertise and capabilities, so the value delivered by assigning a specific team to a specific project varies. The firm wants to maximize the total value delivered across all assignments.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total value delivered across all team-project assignments
Decision variables: active[tm,p]: 1 if team tm is assigned to project p, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: project_value[tm,p]: value delivered when team tm works on project p; max_projects[tm]: maximum number of projects team tm can handle simultaneously
Constraint: Each project must be assigned to at least one team
Constraint: Each team can be assigned to at most their maximum number of concurrent projects

The firm wants to maximize the total value delivered across all assignments.

examples.name: assignment_vehicle_routes
examples.text:
Title: Vehicle-to-Route Assignment
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A logistics company must assign four vehicles to eight delivery routes. Each route has a known cargo load and distance. Each vehicle has a maximum cargo capacity and an operating cost per kilometer. Each route must be covered by exactly one vehicle. The total cargo load across all routes assigned to a vehicle must not exceed that vehicle's capacity. Multiple routes can be assigned to the same vehicle. Determine the minimum-cost assignment of vehicles to routes.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total operating cost: sum of (cost_per_km × distance × assign) across all vehicle-route pairs
Decision variables: assign[v,r]: 1 if vehicle v is assigned to route r, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: route_load[r]: cargo load in tonnes for route r; distance_km[r]: distance in kilometers for route r; vehicle_capacity[v]: maximum cargo capacity in tonnes for vehicle v; cost_per_km[v]: operating cost per kilometer for vehicle v
Constraint: Each route must be assigned to exactly one vehicle
Constraint: The total cargo load assigned to each vehicle must not exceed its capacity

examples.name: bandwidth_allocation

Title: Bandwidth Allocation for Network Sessions
Keywords: sparse filter
Description: A network operator allocates bandwidth to 4 competing sessions on a shared network with 5 links. Each session has a minimum and maximum bandwidth requirement and traverses a fixed set of links (routing matrix). Each link has a capacity that limits the total bandwidth of all sessions using it. Maximize total allocated bandwidth.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total allocated bandwidth = sum of bandwidth[s] over all sessions
Decision variables: bandwidth[s]: bandwidth allocated to session s in Mbps (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: min_rate[s]: minimum required bandwidth for session s; max_rate[s]: maximum useful bandwidth for session s; link_cap[l]: total capacity of link l; uses_link[s,l]: 1 if session s traverses link l, 0 otherwise (routing matrix)
Constraint: Minimum bandwidth: each session receives at least its minimum required rate
Constraint: Maximum bandwidth: each session receives at most its maximum useful rate
Constraint: Link capacity: total bandwidth of all sessions using each link must not exceed the link's capacity

examples.name: beverage_production
examples.text:
Title: Beverage Factory 4-Week Production Planning
Keywords: balance constraint, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A beverage factory plans production over 4 weeks to meet demand at minimum cost. Each week has a demand (1000 boxes), production capacity (1000 boxes), and production cost (1000 yuan per 1000 boxes). Storage cost is 0.2 thousand yuan per 1000 boxes per week. Initial inventory is 0. Minimize total production and storage cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum over all weeks of (prod_cost[t] * produce[t] + 0.2 * inventory[t])
Decision variables: produce[t]: units (1000 boxes) produced in week t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[t]: units (1000 boxes) held in inventory at end of week t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[t]: units (1000 boxes) required in week t; capacity[t]: maximum production units (1000 boxes) in week t; prod_cost[t]: production cost per 1000 boxes in week t (thousand yuan)
Constraint: Inventory balance for week 1 (initial inventory = 0): inventory[w1] = produce[w1] - demand[w1]
Constraint: Inventory balance for weeks 2-4: inventory[t] = inventory[t-1] + produce[t] - demand[t]
Constraint: Production capacity: produce[t] <= capacity[t] for each week

examples.name: bin_packing
examples.text:
Title: Parcel Bin Packing
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A shipping company must pack a set of parcels into standard-size boxes for delivery. Each parcel has a known size (volume). All boxes have the same fixed capacity. The company wants to use as few boxes as possible to minimize shipping overhead. Each parcel must be assigned to exactly one box, and no box may be loaded beyond its capacity. A box is considered used if at least one parcel is assigned to it. Determine which parcels go into which box to minimize the total number of boxes used while ensuring every parcel is packed.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total number of boxes used across all bin assignments
Decision variables: assign[i,b]: 1 if parcel i is packed into box b, 0 otherwise (binary); use_bin[b]: 1 if box b is used, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: item_size[i]: volume/size of parcel i; bin_capacity: maximum volume capacity of each box (all boxes are identical)
Constraint: Each parcel must be assigned to exactly one box
Constraint: The total size of all parcels assigned to a box must not exceed the box's capacity, and the box must be marked as used if any parcel is assigned to it (bin activation linking)

examples.name: blending
examples.text:
Title: Coffee Blending
Keywords: 
Description: A coffee producer must blend three bean types (arabica, robusta, blend_x) to meet volume demand for three product grades (premium, standard, economy). Each product has minimum arabica content and maximum robusta/blend_x fractions. Minimise total bean cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total bean cost across all products
Decision variables: blend[Beans,Products]: kg of bean b used in product p (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: bean_cost[Beans]: cost per kg of each bean type; demand_vol[Products]: required volume (kg) of each product; min_fraction[Beans,Products]: minimum fraction of bean b in product p; max_fraction[Beans,Products]: maximum fraction of bean b in product p
Constraint: Volume met: total beans blended equals product demand
Constraint: Minimum fraction: bean b must contribute at least min_fraction of product p volume
Constraint: Maximum fraction: bean b must contribute at most max_fraction of product p volume

problem.additional_notes: Fraction constraints are linearised using the known total volume: blend[b,p] >= min_fraction[b,p]*demand_vol[p]. Optimal: arabica at minimum, robusta at maximum, blend_x fills remainder. Objective = 395 (premium) + 610 (standard) + 367.5 (economy) = 1372.5.

examples.name: byproduct_lp
examples.text:
Title: By-product LP: Maximize Profit with Sell-or-Dispose Decision
Keywords: balance constraint, no sets
Description: Produce products A and B using two chemical processes. A: 2h process1 + 3h process2. B: 3h process1 + 4h process2. Process1 capacity: 16h. Process2 capacity: 24h. Each unit of B generates 2 units of by-product C at no extra cost. C can be sold (up to 5 units at 3 yuan/unit) or disposed (at -2 yuan/unit cost). Profit: A=4, B=10 yuan/unit. Maximize total profit.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Profit = 4*A + 10*B + 3*C_sold - 2*C_dispose
Decision variables: A: units of product A produced (continuous, >=0); B: units of product B produced (continuous, >=0); C_sold: units of by-product C sold (continuous, 0 <= C_sold <= 5); C_dispose: units of by-product C disposed (continuous, >=0)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Process 1 capacity: 2*A + 3*B <= 16 hours
Constraint: Process 2 capacity: 3*A + 4*B <= 24 hours
Constraint: By-product balance: C_sold + C_dispose = 2*B (all by-product accounted for)
Constraint: Sales limit: C_sold <= 5 units (market limit on by-product C)

Each unit of B generates 2 units of by-product C at no extra cost. C can be sold (up to 5 units at 3 yuan/unit) or disposed (at -2 yuan/unit cost). Profit: A=4, B=10 yuan/unit. Maximize total profit.

Title: Multi-Period Capacity Expansion
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates two plants and must decide in each period whether to invest in expanding a plant's capacity (binary decision). Constraint: Capacity initialisation: first-period capacity = initial_cap + expansion if expanded in p1
Constraint: Capacity update (temporal lag): each period's capacity = previous capacity + new expansion
Constraint: Production upper bound: production cannot exceed current period capacity
Constraint: Demand satisfaction: total production across plants meets demand each period

examples.name: container_nesting
examples.text:
Title: Container Production with Nesting Substitution
Keywords: big-M linking, temporal lag
Description: A plastics factory produces 6 types of containers, ordered by volume (type 1 smallest, type 6 largest). Each type has a per-unit variable production cost and a fixed equipment setup cost (1200 yuan) if any units of that type are produced. Larger containers can substitute for smaller demand: type j (j > i) can fill demand for type i (one unit fills one unit). Goal: minimize total cost while meeting all demand. The demand_satisfaction constraint uses CUMULATIVE demand (sum of demand[j] for j >= i) on the RHS — NOT per-type demand — because each production unit can only fill one demand unit and must cover the aggregated unfilled demand at each level.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of variable production costs + sum of setup costs for activated equipment
Decision variables: produce[i]: integer units of container type i to produce; active[i]: binary, 1 if production equipment for type i is activated (produce[i] > 0); cum_prod[i]: integer, cumulative production from type 1 through type i
Parameters: demand[i]: direct market demand for container type i; cum_demand[i]: cumulative demand from type i onwards = sum(demand[j] for j >= i). MUST be pre-computed and stored as a CSV column.; unit_variable_cost[i]: variable production cost per unit of type i; setup_cost: fixed setup cost per activated equipment (scalar)
Constraint: cum_prod_chain_init: cumulative production of first type = produce[first]
Constraint: cum_prod_chain: for each subsequent type, cum_prod[i] = cum_prod[i-1] + produce[i]
Constraint: demand_satisfaction: for each type i, cumulative production from type i onwards >= cumulative demand from type i onwards (NOT just demand[i])
Constraint: produce_linking: produce[i] <= big_m * active[i] (force setup cost if any production)

Each type has a per-unit variable production cost and a fixed equipment setup cost (1200 yuan) if any units of that type are produced. Larger containers can substitute for smaller demand: type j (j > i) can fill demand for type i (one unit fills one unit). Goal: minimize total cost while meeting all demand. The demand_satisfaction constraint uses CUMULATIVE demand (sum of demand[j] for j >= i) on the RHS — NOT per-type demand — because each production unit can only fill one demand unit and must cover the aggregated unfilled demand at each level.
problem.objective_description: Total cost = sum of variable production costs + sum of setup costs for activated equipment

cum_prod_chain: for each subsequent type, cum_prod[i] = cum_prod[i-1] + produce[i]

produce_linking: produce[i] <= big_m * active[i] (force setup cost if any production)

decision_variables: produce[i]: integer units of container type i to produce
active[i]: binary, 1 if production equipment for type i is activated (produce[i] > 0)
cum_prod[i]: integer, cumulative production from type 1 through type i
parameters: demand[i]: direct market demand for container type i
cum_demand[i]: cumulative demand from type i onwards = sum(demand[j] for j >= i). MUST be pre-computed and stored as a CSV column.
unit_variable_cost[i]: variable production cost per unit of type i
setup_cost: fixed setup cost per activated equipment (scalar)
problem.additional_notes: CRITICAL PATTERN — Nesting/substitution demand: When type j (j > i) can substitute for type i demand, the correct constraint is sum(produce[j] for j >= i) >= sum(demand[j] for j >= i). WRONG: >= demand[i]. The wrong form allows the same production units to simultaneously satisfy multiple demand types (double-counting), making the model trivially cheap. The cum_demand parameter stores the precomputed cumulative demand and must be included as a column in the containers CSV. The cum_prod variable enables the expression cum_prod[ContainerTypes[-1]] - (cum_prod[i] - produce[i]) which equals sum(produce[j] for j >= i).

Title: Cross-Docking Distribution Network
Keywords: 
Description: A distributor ships products from several plants to customers via distribution centers (DCs). Unlike a standard warehouse, each DC operates as a cross-dock: all units received must be immediately re-shipped to customers in the same period — no inventory is held at the DC. Plants have limited supply capacity. Customer demand must be met exactly. Determine the shipment volumes on each plant-to-DC and DC-to-customer lane to minimize total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost = sum of per-unit costs on plant-to-DC and DC-to-customer lanes
Decision variables: ship_in[p,d]: units shipped from plant p to DC d (continuous, non-negative); ship_out[d,c]: units shipped from DC d to customer c (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: plant_cap[p]: maximum units that can be shipped out from plant p; demand[c]: demand at customer c; cost_in[p,d]: cost per unit shipped from plant p to DC d; cost_out[d,c]: cost per unit shipped from DC d to customer c
Constraint: Cross-dock balance: total inbound flow to each DC equals total outbound flow (no storage)
Constraint: Plant capacity: total outbound shipments from each plant cannot exceed its supply capacity
Constraint: Demand coverage: total inbound shipments to each customer must exactly meet that customer's demand

examples.text:
Title: Crude Oil Blending MIP: Maximize Profit with Tier Purchasing
Keywords: no sets, ratio constraint, step cost
Description: A refinery blends crude oil A and crude oil B to produce two grades of gasoline (I and II). Initial crude A stock is 500 tons; additional crude A can be purchased in three price tiers (up to 500 tons each at 10000, 8000, 6000 yuan/ton, must fill lower tiers before higher ones). Crude B: 1000 tons available at no explicit cost (already owned). Gasoline I requires at least 50% crude A by weight (uAI >= uBI). Gasoline II requires at least 60% crude A by weight (uAII >= 1.5*uBII). Sell prices: gasoline I at 4800 yuan/ton, gasoline II at 5600 yuan/ton. Maximize profit.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Profit = 4800*(uAI+uBI) + 5600*(uAII+uBII) - 10000*buy1 - 8000*buy2 - 6000*buy3
Decision variables: buy1: tons of crude A purchased at tier-1 price (10000 yuan/ton), 0-500; buy2: tons of crude A purchased at tier-2 price (8000 yuan/ton), 0-500; buy3: tons of crude A purchased at tier-3 price (6000 yuan/ton), 0-500; z2: binary, 1 if any tier-2 purchase is made; z3: binary, 1 if any tier-3 purchase is made; uAI: tons of crude A used in gasoline I (continuous, lb=0); uAII: tons of crude A used in gasoline II (continuous, lb=0); uBI: tons of crude B used in gasoline I (continuous, lb=0); uBII: tons of crude B used in gasoline II (continuous, lb=0)
Parameters:

problem.title: Crude Oil Blending MIP: Maximize Profit with Tier Purchasing
problem.description: A refinery blends crude oil A and crude oil B to produce two grades of gasoline (I and II). Initial crude A stock is 500 tons; additional crude A can be purchased in three price tiers (up to 500 tons each at 10000, 8000, 6000 yuan/ton, must fill lower tiers before higher ones). Crude B: 1000 tons available at no explicit cost (already owned). Gasoline I requires at least 50% crude A by weight (uAI >= uBI). Gasoline II requires at least 60% crude A by weight (uAII >= 1.5*uBII). Sell prices: gasoline I at 4800 yuan/ton, gasoline II at 5600 yuan/ton. Maximize profit.
problem.objective_description: Profit = 4800*(uAI+uBI) + 5600*(uAII+uBII) - 10000*buy1 - 8000*buy2 - 6000*buy3

Crude B usage: uBI + uBII <= 1000
Gasoline I blend: uAI >= uBI (at least 50% crude A)
Gasoline II blend: uAII >= 1.5*uBII (at least 60% crude A)
Tier ordering (buy2): buy2 <= 500*z2
Tier fill 1 (buy1 full if buy2>0): buy1 >= 500*z2
Tier ordering (buy3): buy3 <= 500*z3
Tier fill 2 (buy2 full if buy3>0): buy2 >= 500*z3

buy2: tons of crude A purchased at tier-2 price (8000 yuan/ton), 0-500
buy3: tons of crude A purchased at tier-3 price (6000 yuan/ton), 0-500
z2: binary, 1 if any tier-2 purchase is made
z3: binary, 1 if any tier-3 purchase is made
uAI: tons of crude A used in gasoline I (continuous, lb=0)
uAII: tons of crude A used in gasoline II (continuous, lb=0)
uBI: tons of crude B used in gasoline I (continuous, lb=0)
uBII: tons of crude B used in gasoline II (continuous, lb=0)
problem.additional_notes: Expected obj=5000000. Optimal: buy all 500+500+500=1500 tons A additional + use all 1000 tons B, all for gasoline II: uAII=2000, uBII=1000/1.5... wait, blend_II: uAII >= 1.5*uBII, so uBII <= uAII/1.5. With uAII=1500t-A from purchases + 500t initial = 2000t A available total, uBII <= 2000/1.5=1333. Revenue=5600*(2000+1000)-10000*500-8000*500-6000*500=5600*3000-12000000=16800000-12000000=4800000. Try uAII=1500+500=2000, uBII=1000: check 2000>=1.5*1000=1500 yes. Revenue=5600*3000-24000000=16800000-12000000=4800000. Also try gasoline I: uAI=500, uBI=500: 4800*1000-0=4800000. Let's try maximize: use all 1000t B in gasoline II (5600>4800). uBII=1000, need uAII>=1500. uAII=1500, buy1=500,buy2=500,buy3=0: cost=10000*500+8000*500=9000000, revenue=5600*2500=14000000, profit=5000000. Yes obj=5000000! All-scalar no CSV. Objective constructed left-to-right: subtract(subtract(subtract(sum(multiply(4800,sum(uAI,uBI)),multiply(5600,sum(uAII,uBII))),multiply(10000,buy1)),multiply(8000,buy2)),multiply(6000,buy3)).

Title: Cutting Stock LP: Minimize Paper Waste from Multiple Roll Widths

Description: A paper mill has three orders: 1000m of 0.5m-wide strips, 3000m of 0.7m strips, 2000m of 0.9m strips. Title: Data Center Workload Assignment
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: Assign computing workloads to servers to minimize energy cost. Each workload runs on exactly one server. Servers are activated only if needed (binary). Activated servers incur a fixed power cost. Running a workload on a server incurs a compute cost. CPU and memory capacity limits must be respected.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of server activation costs + sum of workload compute costs
Decision variables: run[Workloads, Servers]: 1 if workload w runs on server sv (binary); active[Servers]: 1 if server sv is powered on (binary)
Parameters: cpu_req[Workloads]: CPU cores needed by each workload; mem_req[Workloads]: GB memory needed by each workload; cpu_cap[Servers]: CPU cores available per server; mem_cap[Servers]: GB memory available per server; server_cost[Servers]: fixed power cost when server is active; run_cost[Workloads, Servers]: compute cost to run workload w on server sv
Constraint: Each workload is assigned to exactly one server
Constraint: CPU capacity: total CPU requirements of workloads on a server cannot exceed CPU capacity * active
Constraint: Memory capacity: total memory requirements of workloads on a server cannot exceed memory capacity * active
Constraint: Activation link: if a workload runs on a server, the server must be active

Title: Two-Stage Stochastic Production (Newsvendor)
Keywords: deviation variables, scenario weighted sum
Description: A producer must commit to production quantities before demand is revealed (first stage). After the scenario is realised, surplus (over-production) incurs a disposal penalty and shortfall (under-production) incurs a lost-sales penalty (second stage). Three demand scenarios with known probabilities. Minimise expected total cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Production cost + expected recourse cost (probability-weighted overage and underage penalties)
Decision variables: produce[Products]: units produced before demand is known (first-stage, continuous); surplus[Products,Scenarios]: over-production in scenario s (second-stage, continuous); shortfall[Products,Scenarios]: under-production in scenario s (second-stage, continuous)
Parameters: prod_cost[Products]: per-unit production cost; overage_cost[Products]: per-unit disposal penalty for surplus; underage_cost[Products]: per-unit lost-sales penalty for shortfall; probability[Scenarios]: scenario probabilities (sum to 1); demand_scen[Products,Scenarios]: demand under each scenario
Constraint: Overage definition: surplus >= produce - demand (per product per scenario)
Constraint: Underage definition: shortfall >= demand - produce (per product per scenario)

examples.name: diet_mixed_integer
examples.text:
Title: Mixed-Integer Diet Problem with Binary Vegetable Selection
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, filter_column subset, integer variable
Description: Mary wants to maximize protein intake for dinner. She can buy proteins (chicken, salmon, tofu) in any continuous quantity (100g units) and vegetables (broccoli, carrots, spinach, bell pepper, mushrooms) in integer packs of 100g. She must select at least 3 different vegetable types (binary selection variable). A linking constraint ensures zero packs are bought for unselected vegetables. Total budget is $20 and total weight must not exceed 800g (8 units of 100g each).
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total protein intake in grams from all selected proteins and vegetables
Decision variables: eat_protein[p]: quantity of protein p in 100g units (continuous, non-negative); eat_veg[v]: integer packs of vegetable v to buy (integer, non-negative); veg_selected[v]: binary, 1 if any packs of vegetable v are bought
Parameters: protein_per_100g[p]: grams of protein per 100g unit of protein food p; cost_per_100g[p]: cost per 100g unit of protein food p; protein_per_pack[v]: grams of protein per 100g pack of vegetable v; cost_per_pack[v]: cost per 100g pack of vegetable v; budget: total spending budget ($20); max_weight_units: maximum total units of food (8 units = 800g); min_veg_types: minimum number of different vegetable types to select (3); big_m: big-M upper bound for linking constraint (equal to max_weight_units)
Constraint: Budget: total cost of all proteins and vegetables does not exceed $20
Constraint: Weight: total weight (sum of all units) does not exceed 8 units (800g)
Constraint: Minimum variety: at least 3 different vegetable types must be selected (sum of veg_selected >= 3)
Constraint: Vegetable upper link: packs bought are zero if not selected (eat_veg[v] <= big_m * veg_selected[v])
Constraint: Vegetable lower link: if vegetable is selected at least 1 pack must be bought (veg_selected[v] <= eat_veg[v])

Description: Healthy Pet Foods Company produces two types of dog food: Meaties and Yummies. Each pack of Meaties uses 2 lbs grain + 3 lbs meat; each Yummies pack uses 3 lbs grain + 1.5 lbs meat. Constraint: Total meat used across all products cannot exceed monthly meat supply
Constraint: Meaties production cannot exceed the special machine monthly capacity of 90,000 packs

Title: Economic Dispatch with Ramp Rate Constraints
Keywords: init constraint, temporal lag
Description: All generators are online. Allocate generation output each period to meet power demand at minimum fuel cost. Ramp rate constraints limit how quickly each generator can change its output between consecutive periods. Minimize total fuel cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total fuel cost = sum of fuel_cost[g]*generate[g,t] over all generators and periods
Decision variables: generate[g,t]: MW output of generator g in period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: fuel_cost[g]: cost per MWh for generator g; min_output[g]: minimum MW output for generator g; max_output[g]: maximum MW output for generator g; ramp_limit[g]: maximum change in MW output per period for generator g; demand[t]: MW demand in period t
Constraint: Power balance: total generation across all generators equals demand each period
Constraint: Minimum generation: each generator produces at least min_output each period
Constraint: Maximum generation: each generator produces at most max_output each period
Constraint: Ramp up init: first-period output is bounded by min_output (no previous state constraint)
Constraint: Ramp up: increase in output from previous period cannot exceed ramp_limit (temporal lag)
Constraint: Ramp down: decrease in output from previous period cannot exceed ramp_limit (temporal lag)

examples.text:
Title: Battery Energy Storage Arbitrage
Keywords: init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A battery storage operator charges and discharges a battery over 12 hourly periods to profit from electricity price differences. Charging consumes energy at the spot price; discharging earns revenue at the spot price. The battery has a maximum state of charge (capacity), maximum charge/discharge rates, and a charging efficiency. Maximize net profit over the 12 periods.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Net revenue = sum over periods of (price * discharge - price * charge)
Decision variables: charge[Periods]: MWh charged in period t (continuous, non-negative); discharge[Periods]: MWh discharged in period t (continuous, non-negative); soc[Periods]: state of charge at end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: price[Periods]: electricity spot price ($/MWh); max_charge_rate: maximum charge rate per period (MWh); max_discharge_rate: maximum discharge rate per period (MWh); capacity: battery energy capacity (MWh); efficiency: charging efficiency (fraction of energy stored); initial_soc: state of charge at start of first period
Constraint: SOC update init: first-period SOC = initial_soc + efficiency*charge[h1] - discharge[h1]
Constraint: SOC update: SOC[t] = SOC[t-1] + efficiency*charge[t] - discharge[t] (temporal lag)
Constraint: Charge rate limit: charge[t] <= max_charge_rate
Constraint: Discharge rate limit: discharge[t] <= max_discharge_rate
Constraint: Capacity limit: SOC[t] <= capacity

examples.name: facility_location
examples.text:
Title: Capacitated Facility Location
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter
Description: A retailer is deciding which distribution facilities to open in order to serve a set of customers. There are several candidate facility locations, each with a known fixed opening cost and a maximum throughput capacity. For each facility-customer pair there is a known per-unit shipping cost. Each customer has a known demand that must be fully served. A facility can only ship to customers if it is open, and its total shipments across all customers cannot exceed its throughput capacity. An open facility may serve any customer, but a closed facility may ship nothing. Choose which facilities to open and how much to ship from each to each customer to minimize total fixed opening costs plus variable shipping costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = fixed opening costs for opened facilities plus per-unit shipping costs times quantities shipped, summed over all facility-customer pairs
Decision variables: open_fac[f]: 1 if facility f is opened, 0 otherwise (binary); assign[f,c]: units shipped from facility f to customer c (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: fixed_cost[f]: one-time fixed cost to open facility f; facility_capacity[f]: maximum total units facility f can ship across all customers; serve_cost[f,c]: per-unit shipping cost from facility f to customer c; demand[c]: units demanded by customer c that must be exactly fulfilled
Constraint: For each customer, total shipments received from all facilities must exactly equal the customer's demand
Constraint: For each facility, total shipments to all customers must not exceed the facility's throughput capacity if it is open, or zero if it is closed (big-M linking)
Constraint: For each facility-customer pair, the amount shipped cannot exceed the customer's demand times whether the facility is open (prevents any flow from a closed facility)

Title: Farm Crop Allocation LP
Keywords: ratio constraint
Description: Tom and Jerry operate a 100-acre farm and must decide how many acres to plant of four crops: corn, wheat, soybeans, and sorghum. Each crop has a different profit per acre. Four constraints govern the allocation: (1) total land equals 100 acres, (2) corn acreage must be at least twice wheat acreage, (3) soybean acreage must be at least half of sorghum acreage, (4) wheat acreage must equal three times sorghum acreage. Maximize total profit.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit from all crops planted across the 100-acre farm
Decision variables: plant[c]: acres of crop c to plant (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: profit_per_acre[c]: profit per acre for crop c
Constraint: Total planted acres across all crops must equal 100
Constraint: Corn acres must be at least twice wheat acres
Constraint: Soybean acres must be at least half of sorghum acres
Constraint: Wheat acres must equal exactly three times sorghum acres

Title: Farm Planning LP: Crops, Livestock, and External Labor
Keywords: scalar variable
Description: A farm has 100 hectares of land and 15,000 yuan capital. Labor available: 3,500 person-days in autumn/winter and 4,000 in spring/summer. Three crops (soybeans, corn, wheat) can be planted; dairy cows and chickens can be raised. Unused labor can be sold externally at 2.1 yuan/day (spring/summer) and 1.8 yuan/day (autumn/winter). Cows require 1.5 ha land and capital 400 yuan each; barn holds max 32 cows. Chickens require no land, capital 3 yuan each; coop holds max 3000 chickens. Maximize total annual net income.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total annual net income from crops, livestock, and externally sold labor
Decision variables: plant[crop]: hectares of each crop to plant (continuous, non-negative); cows: number of dairy cows (continuous, non-negative); chickens: number of chickens (continuous, non-negative); ext_spring: person-days of labor sold externally in spring/summer (continuous, non-negative); ext_autumn: person-days of labor sold externally in autumn/winter (continuous, non-negative)

Constraint: Total land used by crops and cow feed (1.5 ha per cow) cannot exceed 100 hectares
Constraint: Total capital investment in cows (400 yuan each) and chickens (3 yuan each) cannot exceed 15,000 yuan
Constraint: Total spring/summer labor used by crops, cows (50 person-days), chickens (0.3 person-days) plus externally sold labor cannot exceed 4,000 person-days
Constraint: Total autumn/winter labor used by crops, cows (100 person-days), chickens (0.6 person-days) plus externally sold labor cannot exceed 3,500 person-days
Constraint: Number of cows cannot exceed barn capacity of 32
Constraint: Number of chickens cannot exceed coop capacity of 3,000

examples.text:
Title: Fertilizer Production LP
Keywords: no sets
Description: A factory produces two types of fertilizer: liquid and solid. Machine 1 has 2400 minutes/week available; Machine 2 has 2100 minutes/week. Each lot of liquid fertilizer needs 50 min on M1 and 30 min on M2. Each lot of solid needs 24 min on M1 and 33 min on M2. Current inventory: 30 lots liquid, 90 lots solid. Weekly demand: 75 lots liquid, 95 lots solid. Ending inventory must be non-negative. Maximize total ending inventory.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total ending inventory (liquid_end + solid_end) where ending = current + produced - demand
Decision variables: p_L: lots of liquid fertilizer to produce this week (continuous, non-negative); p_S: lots of solid fertilizer to produce this week (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Machine 1 total processing time cannot exceed 2400 minutes per week
Constraint: Machine 2 total processing time cannot exceed 2100 minutes per week
Constraint: Liquid fertilizer produced must be at least 45 lots to cover demand minus current inventory
Constraint: Solid fertilizer produced must be at least 5 lots to cover demand minus current inventory

Each lot of liquid fertilizer needs 50 min on M1 and 30 min on M2. Each lot of solid needs 24 min on M1 and 33 min on M2. Current inventory: 30 lots liquid, 90 lots solid. Weekly demand: 75 lots liquid, 95 lots solid. Ending inventory must be non-negative. Maximize total ending inventory.

problem.additional_notes: All data is hardcoded as constants. No CSV files needed. Ending inventory = current + produced - demand. To ensure non-negative ending: p_L >= 75-30=45, p_S >= 95-90=5. These are encoded as lower bounds on variables. Objective is maximize p_L+p_S (constant offset -50 does not affect optimality). Optimal: p_L=46.25, p_S=5 (M1 binding: 50*46.25+24*5=2312.5+120=2432.5 > 2400 — wait, check again). Actually solve: at p_L=45 (lower bound binding), M1: 50*45+24*p_S<=2400 => 24*p_S<=150 => p_S<=6.25. M2: 30*45+33*p_S<=2100 => 33*p_S<=750 => p_S<=22.73. So p_S=6.25 (M1 binding). Total ending = (45-45)+(6.25-5)=1.25.

examples.name: financial_cash_flow
examples.text:
Title: Financial Cash Flow Management
Keywords: balance constraint, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A company plans borrowing and investment decisions over 8 months. Each month has a known net operating cash flow. The company can borrow short-term at an interest rate or invest surplus cash at a return rate. It must maintain a minimum cash balance each month and stay within a maximum loan limit. Minimize total net interest cost (borrowing cost minus investment return).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total net interest cost = sum over months of (borrow_rate * loan_balance - invest_rate * invest_balance). Investment balance is capped at max_invest to keep the model bounded.
Decision variables: borrow[Months]: short-term borrowing in month t (continuous, non-negative); repay[Months]: loan repayment in month t (continuous, non-negative); invest[Months]: surplus investment in month t (continuous, non-negative); withdraw[Months]: investment withdrawal in month t (continuous, non-negative); loan_balance[Months]: outstanding loan at end of month t (continuous, non-negative); invest_balance[Months]: investment portfolio at end of month t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: net_cash[Months]: operating cash flow each month (can be negative); borrow_rate: monthly interest rate on loans (scalar); invest_rate: monthly return on investments (scalar); max_loan: maximum outstanding loan balance (scalar); min_cash: minimum required cash balance each month (scalar); max_invest: maximum investment portfolio balance each month (scalar)
Constraint: loan_balance_update_init: first-month loan balance equals new borrowing minus repayment
Constraint: loan_balance_update: each month's loan balance equals previous balance plus new borrowing minus repayment (temporal lag)
Constraint: invest_balance_update_init: first-month investment balance equals new investment minus withdrawals
Constraint: invest_balance_update: each month's investment balance equals previous balance plus new investment minus withdrawals (temporal lag)
Constraint: cash_flow_balance: operating cash flow plus borrowing minus repayment plus withdrawals minus investment must meet minimum cash requirement
Constraint: max_loan_limit: outstanding loan balance must not exceed maximum loan limit
Constraint: max_invest_limit: investment portfolio balance must not exceed maximum investment limit

Description: A food factory plans weekly production of bread, cake, and cookies over 5 days. Each product requires specific ingredients per batch (recipe). Ingredient supply is limited each day. Constraint: Ingredient supply limit: total ingredient usage per day cannot exceed available supply

Title: Generalized Assignment: Jobs to Machines
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A manufacturing plant has a set of jobs to schedule and a set of machines to run them on. Each job must be assigned to exactly one machine. Title: Generation Expansion Planning
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A utility decides when to build new generation capacity of three types (coal, gas, solar) over a 5-year planning horizon. Once built, capacity is permanent (it accumulates over time via a lag-based balance). Each year, total generation must meet energy demand. Minimize total investment plus operating costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of build_cost[g]*max_build[g]*build[g,y] (investment) + fuel_cost[g]*generate[g,y] (operating) over all generator types and years
Decision variables: build[g,y]: 1 if new capacity of type g is built in year y (binary); capacity[g,y]: cumulative installed capacity (MW) of type g in year y (continuous); generate[g,y]: energy produced (MWh) by type g in year y (continuous)

examples.text:
Title: Goal Programming — Production Target Deviation
Keywords: deviation variables
Description: A manufacturer wants to produce as close to demand as possible for each product. Due to capacity limits, some products cannot meet demand. Deviation from demand is penalised: a unit shortfall (under-production) costs more than a unit surplus (over-production). Minimise the total weighted deviation from targets.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total weighted deviation (over_penalty*surplus + under_penalty*shortfall) summed over products
Decision variables: produce[Products]: units produced (continuous, non-negative); surplus[Products]: over-production above demand (continuous, non-negative); shortfall[Products]: under-production below demand (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[Products]: target production quantity; max_capacity[Products]: production capacity upper bound; over_penalty[Products]: cost per unit of surplus; under_penalty[Products]: cost per unit of shortfall
Constraint: Deviation balance: produce + shortfall - surplus = demand for each product
Constraint: Capacity: production cannot exceed max capacity

examples.name: grain_trading
examples.text:
Title: Grain Trading Profit Maximization over 3 Months
Keywords: balance constraint, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A trading company buys and sells grain over 3 months to maximize profit. Warehouse capacity: 5000 dan. Initial inventory: 1000 dan. Initial cash: 20000 yuan. End-of-quarter inventory must be >= 2000 dan. Grain bought in month t can only be sold from month t+1 onward (initial stock can be sold in month 1). Cash cannot go negative at any point. Buy/sell prices vary by month.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit = sum over months of (sell_price[t]*sell[t] - buy_price[t]*buy[t])
Decision variables: buy[t]: dan of grain purchased in month t (continuous, non-negative); sell[t]: dan of grain sold in month t (continuous, non-negative); inv[t]: dan of grain in warehouse at end of month t (continuous, non-negative); cash[t]: cash balance at end of month t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: buy_price[t]: purchase price per dan in month t (yuan); sell_price[t]: selling price per dan in month t (yuan)
Constraint: Inventory balance for month 1 (initial inventory = 1000): inv[m1] = 1000 + buy[m1] - sell[m1]
Constraint: Inventory balance for months 2-3: inv[t] = inv[t-1] + buy[t] - sell[t]
Constraint: Sell limit month 1: sell[m1] <= 1000 (can only sell initial stock, not m1 purchases)
Constraint: Sell limit months 2-3: sell[t] <= inv[t-1] (can only sell stock from previous month)
Constraint: Warehouse capacity: inv[t] <= 5000 for each month
Constraint: End-of-quarter inventory: inv[m3] >= 2000
Constraint: Cash balance for month 1 (initial cash = 20000): cash[m1] = 20000 + sell_price[m1]*sell[m1] - buy_price[m1]*buy[m1]
Constraint: Cash balance for months 2-3: cash[t] = cash[t-1] + sell_price[t]*sell[t] - buy_price[t]*buy[t]
Constraint: Cash non-negativity: cash[t] >= 0 (enforced via lower_bound on cash variable)

examples.name: graph_coloring
examples.text:
Title: Graph Coloring
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, duplicate set
Description: A graph consists of nodes connected by edges. The goal is to assign a color to each node such that no two adjacent nodes (connected by an edge) share the same color, using as few distinct colors as possible. This is the minimum vertex coloring problem, a classic combinatorial optimization problem with applications in register allocation, scheduling, and frequency assignment. The instance has 5 nodes forming a triangle (A-B-C) with a path extension (C-D-E).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total number of distinct colors used across all node assignments
Decision variables: x[n,c]: 1 if node n is assigned color c, 0 otherwise (binary); y[c]: 1 if color c is used by at least one node, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: edges[n1,n2]: 1 if nodes n1 and n2 are connected by an edge, 0 otherwise
Constraint: Each node must be assigned exactly one color
Constraint: If a node uses a color, that color must be marked as active
Constraint: No two adjacent nodes (connected by an edge) may share the same color

examples.name: haus_toys
examples.text:
Title: Haus Toys Product Selection MIP
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, implication constraint, mutual exclusion
Description: Haus Toys can manufacture trucks, airplanes, boats, and trains with wood and steel resources. To maximize profit, the company must decide which types of toys to manufacture and in what quantity, subject to three logical constraints: (1) Trucks and trains are mutually exclusive — if trucks are made, trains cannot be, and vice versa. (2) If boats are manufactured, airplanes must also be manufactured. (3) The number of boats cannot exceed the number of trains. 890 units of wood and 500 units of steel are available.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit from all toys manufactured
Decision variables: qty[t]: quantity of toy type t to produce (continuous, non-negative); make[t]: 1 if toy type t is manufactured, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: profit[t]: profit per unit of toy type t; resource_use[t,r]: units of resource r required per toy of type t; resource_limit[r]: total available units of resource r; big_m[t]: big-M upper bound for linking make[t] to qty[t]
Constraint: Total wood used across all toy types cannot exceed 890 units
Constraint: Total steel used across all toy types cannot exceed 500 units
Constraint: If a toy type is manufactured (make=1), quantity can be positive; if not selected (make=0), quantity must be zero (big-M linking)
Constraint: Trucks and trains are mutually exclusive: make[trucks] + make[trains] <= 1
Constraint: Boats imply airplanes: make[boats] <= make[airplanes]
Constraint: Boats quantity cannot exceed trains quantity: qty[boats] <= qty[trains]

examples.name: hub_location
examples.text:
Title: Hub-and-Spoke Network Location
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, duplicate set, exclude diagonal, sparse filter
Description: A logistics company routes shipments from origins to destinations through a hub-and-spoke network. It must decide which of 3 candidate hubs to open (fixed cost). Shipments from each origin are consolidated at one hub, then possibly transferred to another hub before being delivered to destinations. Each hub has a throughput capacity. Minimize total fixed plus transportation costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = hub opening costs + collection costs (origin to hub) + transfer costs (hub to hub) + delivery costs (hub to destination)
Decision variables: open_hub[Hubs]: 1 if hub h is opened (binary); collect[Origins,Hubs]: flow from origin o to hub h (continuous, non-negative); transfer[Hubs,Hubs]: flow from hub h1 to hub h2 (continuous, non-negative, exclude diagonal); deliver[Hubs,Destinations]: flow from hub h to destination d (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: hub_fixed_cost[Hubs]: fixed opening cost per hub; collect_cost[Origins,Hubs]: per-unit cost from origin to hub; transfer_cost[Hubs,Hubs]: per-unit inter-hub transfer cost (sparse, no self-loops); deliver_cost[Hubs,Destinations]: per-unit cost from hub to destination; supply[Origins]: units to ship from each origin; demand[Destinations]: units needed at each destination; hub_capacity[Hubs]: maximum throughput per hub; big_m: large constant for big-M linking constraints (scalar)
Constraint: supply_dispatch: all supply from each origin must be sent to hubs
Constraint: demand_fulfillment: all demand at each destination must be received from hubs
Constraint: hub_flow_balance: at each hub, inflow (from origins + other hubs) equals outflow (to destinations + other hubs)
Constraint: collect_big_m: collection from origin to hub is zero if hub is not open
Constraint: deliver_big_m: delivery from hub to destination is zero if hub is not open
Constraint: hub_capacity_limit: total flow through a hub (inbound) cannot exceed its capacity times its open indicator
Constraint: transfer_big_m: inter-hub transfer is zero if the originating hub is not open

examples.name: inheritance_partition
examples.text:
Title: Noble Estate Inheritance Partition
Keywords: binary variable, minimax objective, no sets, scalar variable
Description: A noble's estate (183000 total value) must be split between two sons. 14 items: painting=25000, bust=5000, vase=20000, porsche=40000, diamond1=12000, diamond2=12000, diamond3=12000, sofa=3000, dog1=3000, dog2=3000, sculpture=10000, boat=15000, harley=10000, furniture=13000. Binary assign[i]=1 means item goes to son2. Dogs must stay together: assign[dog1]=assign[dog2]. Minimize the absolute difference |son2_value - son1_value|.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Absolute difference between the two sons' shares = |2*sum(value*assign) - 183000|
Decision variables: assign[i]: binary, 1 if item i goes to son2 (0 = son1); diff: scalar continuous (lb=0), the absolute value of (son2_total - son1_total)
Parameters: value[i]: monetary value of item i
Constraint: Dogs must stay together: assign[dog1] - assign[dog2] = 0
Constraint: diff >= son2_value - son1_value: diff - 2*sum(value*assign) >= -183000
Constraint: diff >= son1_value - son2_value: diff + 2*sum(value*assign) >= 183000

Title: Single-Product Inventory Planning with Demand Backlogging

Description: A retailer manages a single product over a multi-period planning horizon. In each period the retailer may place an order (up to a maximum order size) to replenish stock. examples.text:
Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Inventory Planning
Keywords: init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A warehouse stocks multiple products over a multi-period planning horizon. Each product has a known per-period demand that must be fully met. Each product has a per-unit ordering cost and a per-unit holding cost for inventory carried between periods. Each product has a known initial inventory level at the start of the horizon. The warehouse has a shared total storage capacity: the combined ending inventory of all products in any period cannot exceed this limit. Determine the ordering plan across all products and periods that minimizes total ordering and holding costs while meeting all demands and never violating the shared storage capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of per-unit ordering costs times units ordered plus per-unit holding costs times ending inventory, summed across all products and periods
Decision variables: order[p,t]: units of product p ordered at the start of period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in inventory at the end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,t]: known demand for product p in period t; order_cost[p]: per-unit ordering cost for product p; holding_cost[p]: per-unit holding cost for product p carried between periods; initial_inventory[p]: units of product p on hand at the start of the planning horizon; warehouse_capacity: maximum total units of all products that can be stored simultaneously
Constraint: For each product in the first period, ending inventory equals the product's initial inventory plus the order quantity minus demand (inventory balance initialization)
Constraint: For each product in each subsequent period, ending inventory equals the previous period's ending inventory plus the order quantity minus demand (temporal lag inventory balance)
Constraint: For each period, the total ending inventory across all products must not exceed the warehouse's shared storage capacity

examples.text:
Title: Multi-Customer Multi-Product Inventory with Safety Stock
Keywords: init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A central warehouse stocks multiple products and serves multiple retail customers over a multi-period planning horizon. Each customer has a known per-period demand for each product that must be fully met from the warehouse. The warehouse places replenishment orders each period at a per-unit ordering cost. Inventory held at the end of each period incurs a per-unit holding cost. Each product has a minimum safety stock level that must be maintained at the end of every period as a buffer against uncertainty. The warehouse has a shared total storage capacity: the combined ending inventory of all products in any period cannot exceed this limit. Determine the ordering plan across all products and periods that minimizes total ordering and holding costs while meeting all customer demands, honoring safety stock requirements, and never violating the shared storage capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of per-unit ordering costs times units ordered plus per-unit holding costs times ending inventory, summed across all products and periods
Decision variables: order[p,t]: units of product p ordered at the start of period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in inventory at the end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[c,p,t]: known demand of customer c for product p in period t; order_cost[p]: per-unit ordering cost for product p; holding_cost[p]: per-unit holding cost for product p carried between periods; initial_inventory[p]: units of product p on hand at the start of the planning horizon; safety_stock[p]: minimum ending inventory that must be maintained for product p in every period; warehouse_capacity: maximum total units of all products that can be stored simultaneously
Constraint: For each product in the first period, ending inventory equals the product's initial inventory plus the order quantity minus total demand from all customers (inventory balance initialization)
Constraint: For each product in each subsequent period, ending inventory equals the previous period's ending inventory plus the order quantity minus total demand from all customers (temporal lag inventory balance)
Constraint: For each product in each period, the ending inventory must be at least the product's safety stock level
Constraint: For each period, the total ending inventory across all products must not exceed the warehouse's shared storage capacity

Title: Multi-Period Investment Portfolio Rebalancing
Keywords: balance constraint, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: An investor rebalances a portfolio over 4 quarters by buying and selling assets. Holdings evolve via temporal balance: hold[t] = hold[t-1] + buy[t] - sell[t]. Constraint: Holdings balance: hold[a,q] = hold[a,q-1] + buy[a,q] - sell[a,q]
Constraint: Holdings stay within target_units +/- deviation_units
Constraint: Holdings, buys, and sells are non-negative

examples.name: job_shop_scheduling
examples.text:
Title: Open Shop Scheduling — Minimize Makespan
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, duplicate set, exclude diagonal, scalar variable
Description: Four jobs must each be processed on three machines. Each job-machine combination has a known processing time. On each machine, jobs are processed one at a time (no overlap). The order of machines within each job is flexible (open shop). Minimize the makespan (time when all jobs finish).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Makespan: the time by which all jobs have finished on all machines
Decision variables: start[Jobs,Machines]: start time of job j on machine m (continuous, non-negative); before[Jobs,Jobs,Machines]: 1 if job i is processed before job j on machine m (binary, exclude diagonal); makespan: overall completion time (scalar continuous)
Parameters: proc_time[Jobs,Machines]: processing time of job j on machine m; big_m: large constant for disjunctive big-M constraints (scalar)
Constraint: no_overlap_fwd: if job i precedes job j on machine m (before[i,j,m]=1), then job j cannot start until job i finishes
Constraint: no_overlap_rev: if job j precedes job i on machine m (before[i,j,m]=0), then job i cannot start until job j finishes
Constraint: makespan_bound: makespan >= start[j,m] + proc_time[j,m] for all jobs and machines

Description: A retailer orders multiple products from a common supplier over 6 weekly periods. A joint ordering cost is incurred whenever any product is ordered. examples.name: leontief_gdp
examples.text:
Title: Leontief GDP Maximization (Carelland)
Keywords: 
Description: Maximize Carelland's GDP (value added) by choosing production quantities of 4 commodities: steel, engines, electronics, plastic. Value-added coefficients (yuan/ton): steel=208, engines=623, electronics=170, plastic=740. Labor requirements (person-months/ton): steel=6, engines=12, electronics=6, plastic=24. Capacity constraints: engines<=650000, plastic<=60000. Total labor available: 830000 person-months.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total GDP = sum over commodities of va_coeff[c] * x[c]
Decision variables: x[c]: production quantity of commodity c in tons (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: va_coeff[c]: value-added coefficient for commodity c (yuan per ton); labor_pm[c]: labor requirement for commodity c (person-months per ton)
Constraint: Engine production capacity: x[engines] <= 650000
Constraint: Plastic production capacity: x[plastic] <= 60000
Constraint: Total labor constraint: sum_c(labor_pm[c]*x[c]) <= 830000

examples.name: lot_sizing
examples.text:
Title: Capacitated Lot Sizing Problem (CLSP)
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer produces several products on a shared machine over a multi-period planning horizon. In each period, a product can only be produced if the machine is set up for it, incurring a fixed setup cost. Variable production cost and per-unit holding cost also apply. The machine has a limited total capacity per period shared across all products. Known demand must be met each period from available inventory. Determine which products to set up and how much to produce each period to minimize total setup, production, and holding costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of setup costs (when machine is set up for a product) plus variable production costs plus inventory holding costs, over all products and periods
Decision variables: produce[p,t]: units of product p produced in period t (continuous, non-negative); setup[p,t]: 1 if product p is set up on the machine in period t, else 0 (binary); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in inventory at the end of period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,t]: known demand for product p in period t; setup_cost[p]: fixed cost incurred when the machine is set up for product p; prod_cost[p]: variable production cost per unit of product p; holding_cost[p]: per-unit per-period holding cost for product p; initial_inv[p]: inventory on hand at the start of the planning horizon for product p; max_batch[p]: maximum units of product p producible per period (big-M for setup link); machine_cap: total machine capacity (units) available per period, shared across all products
Constraint: Inventory balance initialization: first-period ending inventory equals initial inventory plus production minus demand
Constraint: Inventory balance: ending inventory equals previous inventory plus production minus demand (temporal lag)
Constraint: Setup link: production quantity is zero unless the machine is set up (big-M linking constraint)
Constraint: Machine capacity: total production across all products in a period must not exceed the machine capacity

Determine which products to set up and how much to produce each period to minimize total setup, production, and holding costs.

examples.name: make_or_buy
examples.text:
Title: Make-or-Buy Sourcing Decision
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A manufacturer must decide, for each product, whether to produce it in-house or purchase it from an external supplier. Producing a product in-house incurs a fixed setup cost plus a variable cost per unit; outsourcing incurs only a per-unit purchase price. All demand must be met. In-house production consumes shared labor capacity, so the total production volume across all products cannot exceed the available labor hours. Determine which products to make in-house and how much of each to produce or buy to minimize total cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of (fixed setup cost × make decision + variable production cost × produced units + purchase cost × bought units) over all products
Decision variables: produce[p]: units of product p produced in-house (continuous, non-negative); buy[p]: units of product p purchased externally (continuous, non-negative); make[p]: 1 if product p is produced in-house, else 0 (binary)
Parameters: demand[p]: total demand for product p; prod_cost[p]: variable in-house production cost per unit of product p; fixed_cost[p]: fixed setup cost for producing product p in-house; buy_cost[p]: cost per unit of product p purchased externally; prod_cap[p]: maximum in-house production quantity for product p (also serves as big-M for make-link); labor_cap: total labor capacity available for in-house production (shared across all products)
Constraint: Demand met: produced plus purchased quantity must equal demand for each product
Constraint: Make-link: production quantity is zero unless the product is made in-house (big-M linking constraint using prod_cap as upper bound)
Constraint: Labor capacity: total production across all products must not exceed available labor capacity

examples.text:
Title: Mall Leasing MIP: Maximize Rental Income with Piecewise Profit per Store Count
Keywords: binary variable, mutual exclusion, pre-enumerated options, step cost
Description: Shopping mall has 5000m² to lease across 5 store types: Jewelry (min 1, max 3 shops, 250m²/shop), Shoes&Hats (min 1, max 2, 350m²), General Merchandise (min 1, max 3, 800m²), Bookstore (min 0, max 2, 400m²), Catering (min 1, max 3, 500m²). Profit per store varies with total count of that type (tiered). Rent = 20% of profit. Each valid (type, count) combination is an 'option'. Exactly one option must be chosen per store type. Maximize total rental income.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total rental = sum(annual_rental[o] * y[o]) for all options
Decision variables: y[o]: binary, 1 if option o (a specific type+count combination) is chosen
Parameters: annual_rental[o]: rental income for option o = 0.2 * per_store_profit * count; area_used[o]: total floor area consumed by option o = area_per_shop * count; type_match[o,s]: 1 if option o belongs to store type s, else 0
Constraint: For each store type, exactly one count-level option is chosen: sum(type_match[o,s]*y[o] over Options) = 1 for each StoreType s
Constraint: Total area: sum(area_used[o]*y[o]) <= 5000

examples.text:
Title: Method Selection MIP: Minimize Weekly Labor Cost with Worker Policy Constraints
Keywords: binary variable, mutual exclusion, ratio constraint
Description: A factory must complete 3 tasks (T1, T2, T3), each with two possible methods (A or B). Exactly one method must be chosen per task. Workers are hired at 100 yuan/week (skilled) or 80 yuan/week (laborers). Constraints: total skilled workers <= 400, total laborers <= 800, skilled workers <= 60% of laborers (policy). Additionally, methods T1-B and T3-A cannot both be selected. Minimize total weekly labor cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total weekly labor cost = sum over tasks and methods of method_cost[t,m] * method[t,m]
Decision variables: method[t,m]: binary, 1 if task t is executed using method m, 0 otherwise
Parameters: method_cost[t,m]: total weekly labor cost if task t uses method m; skilled_req[t,m]: number of skilled workers required if task t uses method m; laborer_req[t,m]: number of laborers required if task t uses method m
Constraint: One method per task: sum over Methods of method[t,m] = 1 for each task
Constraint: Max 400 skilled workers: sum(skilled_req[t,m]*method[t,m]) <= 400
Constraint: Max 800 laborers: sum(laborer_req[t,m]*method[t,m]) <= 800
Constraint: Skilled <= 60% of laborers: sum(skilled_req*method) - 0.6*sum(laborer_req*method) <= 0
Constraint: Mutual exclusion: method[T1,B] + method[T3,A] <= 1

examples.text:
Title: Multi-Sourcing Procurement with Supplier Allocation Limits
Keywords: 
Description: A buyer procures several items from multiple suppliers. Each supplier offers different unit costs per item and has a total supply capacity. Additionally, each supplier-item combination has a maximum allocation limit (e.g., due to supplier contracts or risk-spreading policies). All demand must be met exactly. Determine how much of each item to order from each supplier to minimize total procurement cost while respecting supplier capacities and per-source allocation limits.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total procurement cost = sum of unit cost times order quantity over all supplier-item pairs
Decision variables: order[s,i]: quantity of item i ordered from supplier s (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[i]: total demand for item i; unit_cost[s,i]: cost per unit of item i sourced from supplier s; capacity[s]: maximum total units that supplier s can supply across all items; max_qty[s,i]: maximum quantity of item i that may be sourced from supplier s
Constraint: Demand coverage: total quantity ordered across all suppliers for each item must exactly meet demand
Constraint: Supplier capacity: total quantity supplied by each supplier across all items must not exceed that supplier's capacity
Constraint: Allocation limit: quantity ordered from a specific supplier for a specific item must not exceed the per-source maximum

Title: Multicommodity Network Flow
Keywords: duplicate set, exclude diagonal, sparse filter
Description: A network operator routes multiple traffic demands (commodities) over a shared 5-node network with 8 directed arcs. Each commodity has a source node with positive supply and a destination node with negative supply; transit nodes have zero supply. Each arc has a capacity shared across all commodities. Minimize total routing cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum over all commodities and arcs of arc_cost[i,j]*flow[k,i,j]

Constraint: Flow conservation: for each commodity-node pair, outflow minus inflow equals net supply (positive at source, negative at destination, zero at transit)
Constraint: Arc capacity: total flow across all commodities on each arc must not exceed arc capacity

Title: Fixed-Charge Network Design
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter, duplicate set, sparse filter
Description: A telecom operator decides which links to build in a potential 5-node network topology and how to route aggregated traffic. Each potential link has a fixed construction cost, a per-unit traffic cost, and a capacity limit. Traffic must flow from sources (A: +50, B: +30) to the sink (E: -80). Transit nodes (C, D) have zero net demand. Minimize total fixed plus variable costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of fixed_cost[i,j]*build[i,j] + flow_cost[i,j]*flow[i,j] over all potential links

Constraint: Flow conservation: outflow minus inflow at each node equals net demand
Constraint: Capacity-big-M link: flow on each built link cannot exceed link capacity (if not built, flow must be zero)

examples.name: network_production_inventory_transportation
examples.text:
Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network
Keywords: domain filter, init constraint, sparse filter, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set), each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period throughput capacity. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period arc capacity. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, and ending inventory levels at each plant and warehouse to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, and transportation costs across all arcs and periods.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: production costs at plants, inventory holding costs at plants and warehouses, and per-unit shipping costs on all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, summed across all valid arcs and periods
Decision variables: produce[i,t]: units produced at plant i in period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_plant[i,t]: inventory held at plant i at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_wh[w,t]: inventory held at warehouse w at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); flow_pw[i,w,t]: units shipped from plant i to warehouse w in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs); flow_wr[w,r,t]: units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs)
Parameters: prod_cost[i]: production cost per unit at plant i; prod_capacity[i]: maximum units that can be produced at plant i in any single period; hold_cost_plant[i]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at plant i; initial_inv_plant[i]: inventory held at plant i at the start of the planning horizon (before period t0); hold_cost_wh[w]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at warehouse w; wh_capacity[w]: maximum inventory units that can be stored at warehouse w at the end of any period; initial_inv_wh[w]: inventory held at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon; demand[r,t]: units required by retailer r in period t, which must be exactly fulfilled; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: maximum units shippable from plant i to warehouse w in a single period (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: maximum units shippable from warehouse w to retailer r in a single period (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at plant i equals initial inventory plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses in period t0
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at plant i in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at warehouse w equals initial inventory plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers in period t0
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at warehouse w in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers
Constraint: Production at each plant in each period must not exceed the plant's per-period production capacity
Constraint: Inventory held at each warehouse at the end of each period must not exceed the warehouse's storage capacity
Constraint: For each retailer and period, total inflow from all connected warehouses must exactly equal the retailer's demand
Constraint: Flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity
Constraint: Flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity
