examples.text:
Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Bill of Materials
Keywords: BOM parameter, domain filter, init constraint, sparse filter, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. Multiple finished products are produced and distributed. At each plant, producing a unit of each finished product requires specific quantities of raw material components according to a Bill of Materials (BOM). Plants procure components from external suppliers each period at a per-unit component cost and hold component inventory between periods at a per-unit component holding cost. Each period, plants consume components according to BOM requirements to produce finished goods. Finished goods inventory at each plant incurs a per-unit holding cost per period. Total production across all products at each plant is bounded by the plant's per-period production capacity. From each plant, finished goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set), each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period throughput capacity shared across all products. Warehouses hold finished goods inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a shared storage capacity across all products. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period arc capacity shared across all products. Each retailer has a known demand for each product each period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose component procurement quantities, production quantities per product, inter-tier shipments, and inventory levels at each plant and warehouse to minimize total cost: component procurement costs, component and finished-goods holding costs at plants, warehouse holding costs, and transportation costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: component procurement costs at plants, component holding costs at plants, finished-goods holding costs at plants and warehouses, and per-unit shipping costs on all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, summed across all products and periods
Decision variables: comp_purchase[i,c,t]: units of component c purchased at plant i in period t (continuous, non-negative); comp_inventory[i,c,t]: units of component c held at plant i at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); produce[i,p,t]: units of finished product p produced at plant i in period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_plant[i,p,t]: units of finished product p held at plant i at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_wh[w,p,t]: units of finished product p held at warehouse w at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); flow_pw[i,w,p,t]: units of product p shipped from plant i to warehouse w in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs); flow_wr[w,r,p,t]: units of product p shipped from warehouse w to retailer r in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs)
Parameters: bom[c,p]: units of component c required to produce one unit of finished product p; comp_cost[c]: per-unit procurement cost for component c; comp_hold_cost[c]: per-unit holding cost per period for component c stored at any plant; initial_comp_inv[i,c]: initial inventory of component c at plant i at the start of the planning horizon; prod_capacity[i]: maximum total units (across all products) that can be produced at plant i in any single period; hold_cost_plant[i]: per-unit holding cost per period for finished goods stored at plant i; initial_inv_plant[i,p]: initial inventory of finished product p at plant i at the start of the planning horizon; hold_cost_wh[w]: per-unit holding cost per period for finished goods stored at warehouse w; wh_capacity[w]: maximum total units (across all products) that can be stored at warehouse w at the end of any period; initial_inv_wh[w,p]: initial inventory of finished product p at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon; demand[r,p,t]: units of product p required by retailer r in period t, which must be exactly fulfilled; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w, shared across all products (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r, shared across all products (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: maximum total units (across all products) shippable from plant i to warehouse w per period (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: maximum total units (across all products) shippable from warehouse w to retailer r per period (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: Component inventory balance for the first period: ending component inventory at plant i equals initial component inventory plus components purchased minus components consumed in production (BOM quantity times units produced, summed over all finished products)
Constraint: Component inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending component inventory at plant i in period t equals prior-period ending inventory plus components purchased minus components consumed
Constraint: Finished-goods inventory balance for the first period: ending finished-goods inventory of product p at plant i equals initial inventory plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses
Constraint: Finished-goods inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending finished-goods inventory of product p at plant i in period t equals prior-period ending inventory plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory of product p at warehouse w equals initial inventory plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory of product p at warehouse w in period t equals prior-period ending inventory plus inflow from plants minus outflow to retailers
Constraint: Total production across all products at each plant in each period must not exceed the plant's per-period production capacity
Constraint: Total finished-goods inventory across all products at each warehouse at the end of each period must not exceed the warehouse's storage capacity
Constraint: For each retailer, product, and period, total inflow from all connected warehouses must exactly equal the retailer's demand
Constraint: For each plant-to-warehouse arc in each period, total flow across all products must not exceed the arc's per-period throughput capacity
Constraint: For each warehouse-to-retailer arc in each period, total flow across all products must not exceed the arc's per-period throughput capacity

Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with BOM and Work Centers
Keywords: BOM parameter, domain filter, init constraint, sparse filter, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods, producing multiple finished products. Each plant contains two types of work centers: component work centers (CompWCs) and finished-product work centers (FinWCs). Component work centers produce raw material components in-house; each has its own per-period capacity (total units across all components) and a per-unit production cost. Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Plant Opening, Closing, and Step Operating Costs
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter, init constraint, sparse filter, step cost, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. Each plant starts the horizon in a known initial state (open or closed). In each period, each plant is either open or closed. A plant may be opened or closed any number of times within the horizon. Opening a plant (transitioning from closed to open) incurs a one-time opening cost in that period. Closing a plant (transitioning from open to closed) incurs a one-time closing cost in that period. When a plant is open it incurs a per-period step operating cost that depends on its production tier (low, medium, or high), each tier covering a range of output levels. When a plant is closed it incurs no operating cost and cannot produce. In each period, each open plant selects exactly one tier; closed plants select no tier. Within the selected tier, the actual production quantity can range freely between the tier's lower and upper bounds, and each unit also incurs a per-unit production cost. Produced goods enter plant inventory; a holding cost applies to every unit stored at a plant at period end. Goods are shipped from plants to warehouses and from warehouses to retailers over a sparse set of established arcs, each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period arc capacity. Warehouses hold inventory across periods at a holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity. Each retailer has a known demand per period that must be exactly met. The goal is to decide when to open and close each plant, which tier each open plant uses each period, how much to produce, and how to route goods to minimise total cost: plant opening costs, plant closing costs, step operating costs, per-unit production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, and transportation costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: one-time plant opening costs (charged each time a plant opens), one-time plant closing costs (charged each time a plant closes), per-period step operating costs based on the active production tier, per-unit production costs, inventory holding costs at plants and warehouses, and per-unit shipping costs across all arcs and periods

Parameters: opening_cost[i]: one-time fixed cost incurred each time plant i is activated (transitions from closed to open); closing_cost[i]: one-time fixed cost incurred each time plant i is deactivated (transitions from open to closed); initial_open[i]: 1 if plant i is open at the start of the planning horizon, 0 if closed; prod_cost[i]: variable production cost per unit produced at plant i; hold_cost_plant[i]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at plant i; initial_inv_plant[i]: inventory at plant i at the start of the planning horizon; tier_lb[i,k]: minimum production quantity required when plant i operates at tier k; tier_ub[i,k]: maximum production quantity allowed when plant i operates at tier k; tier_op_cost[i,k]: fixed operating cost per period when plant i is in tier k; hold_cost_wh[w]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at warehouse w; wh_capacity[w]: maximum inventory that can be held at warehouse w at end of any period; initial_inv_wh[w]: inventory at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon; demand[r,t]: units required by retailer r in period t; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: per-period arc capacity from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: per-period arc capacity from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: For the first period: if a plant starts closed (initial_open=0) and is open in period t0, plant_opens must equal 1; ensured by plant_opens[i,t0] + initial_open[i] >= open_plant[i,t0]
Constraint: For each subsequent period: if a plant was closed in t-1 and is open in t, plant_opens must equal 1; ensured by plant_opens[i,t] + open_plant[i,t-1] >= open_plant[i,t]
Constraint: For the first period: if a plant starts open (initial_open=1) and is closed in period t0, plant_closes must equal 1; ensured by plant_closes[i,t0] + open_plant[i,t0] >= initial_open[i]
Constraint: For each subsequent period: if a plant was open in t-1 and is closed in t, plant_closes must equal 1; ensured by plant_closes[i,t] + open_plant[i,t] >= open_plant[i,t-1]
Constraint: For each plant and period, exactly one production tier must be active if the plant is open, and no tier may be active if it is closed (sum of tier indicators equals open status)
Constraint: Production at each open plant in each period must be at least the lower bound of the active tier
Constraint: Production at each open plant in each period must not exceed the upper bound of the active tier
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory equals initial inventory plus production minus total shipments to warehouses
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory equals prior-period ending inventory plus production minus total shipments to warehouses
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory equals initial inventory plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory equals prior-period ending inventory plus inflow from plants minus outflow to retailers
Constraint: Inventory held at each warehouse at end of each period must not exceed the warehouse storage capacity
Constraint: For each retailer and period, total inflow from all connected warehouses must exactly equal the retailer's demand
Constraint: Flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity
Constraint: Flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity

Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Plant Opening and Step Operating Costs
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter, init constraint, sparse filter, step cost, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer must decide when to activate plants and how to operate a three-tier distribution network over multiple time periods. A plant can be opened in any period; once opened, it remains open for the rest of the planning horizon and cannot be closed. Opening a plant incurs a one-time fixed cost charged in the period it first becomes active. Once a plant is open, it incurs a per-period step operating cost that depends on how much it produces: production is divided into tiers (low, medium, high), each tier covering a range of output levels and carrying a fixed operating cost per period. In each period, a plant operates in exactly one tier (or not at all if not yet opened). Within the selected tier, the actual production quantity can range freely between the tier's lower and upper bounds, and each unit produced also incurs a per-unit production cost. Produced goods are added to plant inventory; a holding cost applies to every unit stored at a plant at period end. Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter, init constraint, integer variable, sparse filter, step cost, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set). Each arc offers quantity-discount pricing: the per-unit shipping cost decreases as the shipment volume moves into higher volume tiers, and each shipment dispatched on an arc incurs a fixed charge. An arc has a fixed shipment size (e.g. truck capacity), so the number of dispatches required in a period equals the ceiling of total flow divided by shipment size. Total fixed cost for an arc in a period is therefore fixed_cost_per_shipment times the number of shipments. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with the same tier-based pricing and multi-shipment fixed-charge structure. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, tier selections, shipment counts, and ending inventory levels to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, variable tier-based shipping costs on all arcs, and total fixed shipment charges across all arcs and periods.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: production costs at plants, inventory holding costs at plants and warehouses, variable per-unit tier shipping costs (summed over active tier flows), and total fixed shipment charges (fixed_cost_per_shipment times number of shipments) on all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, summed across all valid arcs and periods

Parameters: prod_cost[i]: production cost per unit at plant i; prod_capacity[i]: maximum units that can be produced at plant i in any single period; hold_cost_plant[i]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at plant i; initial_inv_plant[i]: inventory held at plant i at the start of the planning horizon; hold_cost_wh[w]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at warehouse w; wh_capacity[w]: maximum inventory units that can be stored at warehouse w at end of any period; initial_inv_wh[w]: inventory held at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon; demand[r,t]: units required by retailer r in period t, which must be exactly fulfilled; tier_lb_pw[i,w,tier]: lower bound on flow volume for pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); tier_ub_pw[i,w,tier]: upper bound on flow volume for pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); tier_cost_pw[i,w,tier]: per-unit shipping cost in pricing tier on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); tier_lb_wr[w,r,tier]: lower bound on flow volume for pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r); tier_ub_wr[w,r,tier]: upper bound on flow volume for pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r); tier_cost_wr[w,r,tier]: per-unit shipping cost in pricing tier on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r); fixed_cost_pw[i,w]: fixed charge per dispatch on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); total fixed cost = fixed_cost_pw * num_shipments_pw; fixed_cost_wr[w,r]: fixed charge per dispatch on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r); total fixed cost = fixed_cost_wr * num_shipments_wr; shipment_size_pw[i,w]: maximum units per dispatch on plant-to-warehouse arc (i,w); flow <= shipment_size_pw * num_shipments_pw; shipment_size_wr[w,r]: maximum units per dispatch on warehouse-to-retailer arc (w,r)

Title: Three-Tier Distribution Network Flow
Keywords: domain filter, sparse filter
Description: A logistics company operates a three-tier distribution network: manufacturing plants ship goods to regional warehouses, which then forward them to end retailers. Each plant has a maximum supply capacity. Each retailer has a fixed demand that must be exactly met. Arcs between tiers have both a per-unit shipping cost and a throughput capacity limit. Not all plant-warehouse and warehouse-retailer pairs have established shipping lanes — only arcs present in the cost tables are valid. Flow must be conserved at each warehouse: total inflow from plants must equal total outflow to retailers. Find the minimum-cost flow plan that satisfies all retailer demands without violating any arc or plant capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost across all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, weighted by flow volume on each arc
Decision variables: flow_pw[i,w]: units shipped from plant i to warehouse w (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs); flow_wr[w,r]: units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs)
Parameters: supply[i]: maximum supply available at plant i; demand[r]: demand that must be exactly fulfilled at retailer r; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: maximum throughput capacity on the arc from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: maximum throughput capacity on the arc from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: Total flow shipped out of each plant across all outgoing arcs must not exceed that plant's supply capacity
Constraint: Total flow received by each retailer across all incoming arcs must exactly equal that retailer's demand
Constraint: For each warehouse, total flow arriving from all plants must equal total flow departing to all retailers (flow conservation)
Constraint: Flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc must not exceed that arc's capacity
Constraint: Flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc must not exceed that arc's capacity

Constraint: OR capacity: total duration of assigned surgeries per OR cannot exceed OR capacity
Constraint: Surgeon workload: total duration of assigned surgeries per surgeon cannot exceed surgeon capacity

Title: Car Parking Minimax: Minimize Maximum Side Length
Keywords: binary variable, minimax objective, scalar variable
Description: 15 cars must be parked on either side A or side B of a street. Each car has a known length. The total occupied street length on each side is the sum of lengths of cars parked there. Minimize the maximum occupied length across both sides, so that the total street block required is as short as possible. All 15 cars must be parked (each on exactly one side).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Maximum total occupied length across the two sides of the street
Decision variables: side[c]: 1 if car c parks on side A, 0 if on side B (binary); max_len: maximum occupied length across both sides (scalar continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: car_length[c]: length of car c in meters
Constraint: The total length of cars on side A must not exceed the minimax variable max_len
Constraint: The total length of cars on side B (total_length - side_A) must not exceed max_len

examples.name: perishable_inventory
examples.text:
Title: Perishable Inventory Planning with Expiry Waste
Keywords: init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A retailer manages several perishable products (e.g., fresh food) over a daily planning horizon. Purchased goods can be held for at most one period before they expire; any unsold inventory from the previous period must be wasted. Demand must be satisfied each day. The retailer incurs a purchase cost per unit bought, a holding cost per unit carried overnight (end-of-period inventory), and a waste penalty per unit discarded. Determine daily purchase quantities to minimize total cost while ensuring demand is met and no inventory is held past its shelf life.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = purchase cost + holding cost for overnight inventory + waste penalty for expired units, summed over all products and periods
Decision variables: purchase[p,t]: units of product p purchased in period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in storage at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); waste[p,t]: units of product p expired/wasted in period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,t]: demand for product p in period t; purchase_cost[p]: cost per unit purchased for product p; holding_cost[p]: cost per unit held overnight for product p; waste_penalty[p]: penalty per unit wasted/expired for product p; initial_inventory[p]: units of product p on hand at the start of the planning horizon (age 1, will expire in period 1 if not used); storage_cap[p]: maximum units of product p that can be stored overnight
Constraint: Balance initialization: first-period inventory plus waste plus demand equals initial inventory plus purchases
Constraint: Balance: current inventory plus waste plus demand equals previous inventory plus purchases (temporal lag)
Constraint: Expiry (shelf-life = 1 period): end-of-period inventory cannot exceed units purchased in that period — forcing old stock to be wasted
Constraint: Storage capacity: end-of-period inventory for each product must not exceed the storage limit

Title: Personnel Selection MIP: Minimize Salary with Skill and Experience Requirements
Keywords: binary variable, mutual exclusion, ratio constraint
Description: 5 candidates F,G,H,I,J with salaries 12k,15k,18k,5k,10k. Budget ≤ 40k, max 4 employees. Need total skill ≥ 8, total experience ≥ 8. G and J have similar backgrounds so at most one can be hired. Minimize total salary.

Objective description: Total salary = sum(salary[c] * hire[c]) over all candidates

Constraint: Max employees: sum(hire) <= 4
Constraint: Skill requirement: sum(skill_level * hire) >= 8
Constraint: Experience requirement: sum(experience * hire) >= 8
Constraint: G and J mutual exclusion: hire[G] + hire[J] <= 1

examples.name: portfolio_investment_lp
examples.text:
Title: Multi-Year Investment Portfolio Optimization
Keywords: balance constraint, no sets, temporal lag
Description: A company has 300,000 yuan starting capital to invest over 3 years. Four investment options: Project 1 (annual, 20% return, renewable each year), Project 2 (year 1 only, 50% return at end of year 2, cap 150,000), Project 3 (year 2 only, 60% return at end of year 3, cap 200,000), Project 4 (year 3 only, 40% return at end of year 3, cap 100,000). Uninvested cash earns nothing. Maximize total wealth at end of year 3.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total wealth at end of year 3 = 1.2*x1_3 + 1.4*x4 + k3 + 1.6*x3
Decision variables: x1_1: amount invested in project 1 at start of year 1 (continuous, non-negative); x1_2: amount invested in project 1 at start of year 2 (continuous, non-negative); x1_3: amount invested in project 1 at start of year 3 (continuous, non-negative); x2: amount invested in project 2 at start of year 1 (continuous, non-negative); x3: amount invested in project 3 at start of year 2 (continuous, non-negative); x4: amount invested in project 4 at start of year 3 (continuous, non-negative); k1: cash held uninvested after year 1 decisions (continuous, non-negative); k2: cash held uninvested after year 2 decisions (continuous, non-negative); k3: cash held uninvested after year 3 decisions (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Year 1 balance: x1_1 + x2 + k1 = 300000
Constraint: Project 2 cap: x2 <= 150000
Constraint: Year 2 balance: x1_2 + x3 + k2 = 1.2*x1_1 + k1
Constraint: Project 3 cap: x3 <= 200000
Constraint: Year 3 balance: x1_3 + x4 + k3 = 1.2*x1_2 + 1.5*x2 + k2
Constraint: Project 4 cap: x4 <= 100000

Title: Portfolio Rebalancing with Transaction Costs
Keywords: balance constraint
Description: An investor holds a current portfolio and wants to rebalance toward target weights. Buying and selling incur transaction costs. The total portfolio value is fixed. Minimize total transaction costs while achieving target allocation within a tolerance band.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total transaction costs from buying and selling assets
Decision variables: hold[Assets]: final units held (continuous, non-negative); buy[Assets]: units purchased (continuous, non-negative); sell[Assets]: units sold (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: current_hold[Assets]: current holdings; price[Assets]: current price per unit; buy_cost[Assets]: transaction cost per unit bought; sell_cost[Assets]: transaction cost per unit sold; target_weight[Assets]: target portfolio fraction; total_value: target total portfolio value; max_deviation: maximum allowed deviation from target weight
Constraint: Balance: final holdings = current holdings + buy - sell
Constraint: Budget: total portfolio value equals target
Constraint: Weight upper bound: asset value <= (target_weight + max_deviation) * total_value
Constraint: Weight lower bound: asset value >= (target_weight - max_deviation) * total_value

examples.text:
Title: Procurement with All-Units Quantity Discounts
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, step cost
Description: A buyer procures several items from a supplier that offers all-units quantity discounts: each item has pricing tiers (small, medium, large) with decreasing unit costs as order volume increases. Within a tier, the unit cost applies to every unit ordered. The buyer must select exactly one tier per item, order at least the tier minimum quantity if that tier is selected, and meet all demand. Determine the tier and order quantity for each item to minimize total procurement cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total procurement cost = sum of unit cost times order quantity across all items and tiers
Decision variables: order_qty[i,k]: quantity of item i ordered under tier k (continuous, non-negative); use_tier[i,k]: 1 if item i is ordered at tier k, else 0 (binary)
Parameters: demand[i]: total demand for item i; unit_cost[i,k]: cost per unit for item i ordered at tier k; tier_lb[i,k]: minimum order quantity for item i under tier k; tier_ub[i,k]: maximum order quantity for item i under tier k
Constraint: Exactly one pricing tier must be selected per item
Constraint: Total order quantity across tiers for each item must meet the item's demand
Constraint: Order quantity at a tier must be at least the tier's minimum order quantity if that tier is selected (lower bound link)
Constraint: Order quantity at a tier must not exceed the tier's maximum order quantity if selected, and is zero if not selected (upper bound link)

examples.name: production
examples.text:
Title: Furniture Factory Multi-Week Production Mix
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, integer variable
Description: A furniture factory produces chairs, tables, and shelves over a multi-week planning horizon. Each product type requires a certain number of labor-hours and board-feet of wood per unit. The factory has a fixed weekly supply of labor hours and wood. Products can only be produced in whole units — no fractional quantities. If the factory decides to include a product type in a given week's production run, it incurs a fixed setup cost and a variable per unit production cost, and the factory must produce at least a minimum batch size for that product type for this week. Each product type also has a maximum weekly production capacity due to machine constraints. Due to changeover constraints, at most two product types can be produced in any given week. Each product type has a revenue per unit produced. Determine which product types to include in the production plan each week and how many units of each to make to maximize total revenue minus total cost across all weeks.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total revenue from production minus total cost (fixed setup cost plus variable per unit production cost) summed across all weeks
Decision variables: produce[p,w]: integer number of units of product p to produce in week w; active[p,w]: binary, 1 if product p is included in week w's production run, 0 otherwise
Parameters: revenue_per_unit[p]: revenue earned per unit of product p sold; production_cost[p]: variable cost per unit of product p produced; labor_hours[p]: labor-hours required to produce one unit of product p; wood_board_feet[p]: board-feet of wood required to produce one unit of product p; setup_cost[p]: fixed cost incurred if product p is included in a week's production run; min_batch[p]: minimum number of units of product p that must be produced if active in a given week; max_batch[p]: maximum number of units of product p that can be produced in a given week; labor_capacity: total labor-hours available per week (shared across all products); wood_capacity: total board-feet of wood available per week (shared across all products)
Constraint: Total labor-hours consumed by all active product types in week w cannot exceed the factory's fixed weekly labor capacity
Constraint: Total board-feet of wood consumed by all active product types in week w cannot exceed the factory's fixed weekly wood supply
Constraint: If product type p is included in week w's production run, at least min_batch[p] units must be produced that week; if not included, production must be zero
Constraint: Production of product type p in week w cannot exceed its maximum weekly machine capacity, and production can only be positive if product type p is active in that week
Constraint: Due to changeover constraints, at most two product types can be active in any given week

Title: Multi-Product Quarterly Production with Backlog Compensation
Keywords: balance constraint, deviation variables, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A factory produces three products (I, II, III) over four quarters. Contract delivery requirements are given per product per quarter. Initial inventory is zero; final inventory must be at least 150 units per product. The factory has 15,000 production hours per quarter. Each unit of product I requires 2 hours, product II 4 hours, product III 3 hours. Product I cannot be produced in Q2 (equipment change). If a delivery is late, the factory pays compensation: 20 yuan/unit/quarter delay for products I and II, 10 yuan/unit/quarter delay for product III. Carrying inventory costs 5 yuan/unit/quarter. Minimize total cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = 5*sum(inventory) + sum(comp_rate[p]*backlog[p,t]) over all products and quarters
Decision variables: produce[p,t]: units of product p produced in quarter t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[p,t]: units of product p held in inventory at end of quarter t (continuous, non-negative); backlog[p,t]: units of product p still owed (not yet delivered) at end of quarter t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,t]: contract delivery requirement for product p in quarter t; hours_per_unit[p]: production hours required per unit of product p; comp_rate[p]: compensation cost in yuan per unit per quarter of delay
Constraint: Inventory balance init (Q1): inventory[p,Q1] - backlog[p,Q1] = produce[p,Q1] - demand[p,Q1], with zero initial stock
Constraint: Inventory balance (Q2-Q4): inventory[p,t] - backlog[p,t] = inventory[p,t-1] - backlog[p,t-1] + produce[p,t] - demand[p,t]
Constraint: Production capacity: total production hours per quarter must not exceed 15,000
Constraint: Product I cannot be produced in Q2: produce[I,Q2] = 0
Constraint: End-of-horizon inventory for each product must be at least 150 units
Constraint: End-of-horizon backlog must be zero (all contracts fulfilled by Q4)

examples.name: production_backorder_workforce
examples.text:
Title: Production Planning with Workforce Management and Backorders
Keywords: balance constraint, deviation variables, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A company makes foldable tables over 6 months (Jan-Jun). Each month, it decides how many units to produce in-house, how many to outsource, how many workers to hire or fire, and how much overtime to use. Demand may exceed supply, creating backorders carried to the next month. A 'sold' variable tracks units sold each period (= demand fulfilled + prior backorders cleared). Maximize total net profit = sum(sales_price * sold[t]) minus all costs. Initial workforce: 1000, initial inventory: 15000. Terminal conditions: ending inventory >= 10000, ending backorder = 0.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total net profit: revenue from all units sold minus all production, labor, and inventory costs
Decision variables: produce[t]: in-house production quantity in month t (continuous, >=0); outsource[t]: outsourced quantity in month t (continuous, >=0); sold[t]: units sold (demand fulfilled) in month t (continuous, >=0); inventory[t]: ending inventory at month t (continuous, >=0); backlog[t]: ending backlog (unfulfilled demand) at month t (continuous, >=0); workforce[t]: workforce level at end of month t (continuous, >=0); hire[t]: new hires in month t (continuous, >=0); fire[t]: firings in month t (continuous, >=0); overtime_hours[t]: total overtime hours in month t (continuous, >=0)
Parameters: demand[t]: forecasted demand in month t; initial_workforce: workforce at start of January; initial_inventory: inventory at start of January; sales_price: revenue per unit sold; raw_material_cost: raw material cost per in-house unit; outsource_cost: all-inclusive cost per outsourced unit; holding_cost: inventory holding cost per unit per month; backorder_penalty: backorder cost per unit per month; labor_per_unit: labor hours required per in-house unit; regular_hours_per_worker: regular working hours per worker per month; regular_wage: wage per regular hour; overtime_wage: wage per overtime hour; max_overtime_per_worker: maximum overtime hours per worker per month; hire_cost: cost to hire one worker; fire_cost: cost to fire one worker; min_terminal_inventory: required ending inventory at end of June
Constraint: Workforce balance (init): workforce[jan] = initial_workforce + hire[jan] - fire[jan]
Constraint: Workforce balance (lag): workforce[t] = workforce[t-1] + hire[t] - fire[t] for t > jan
Constraint: Sold definition (init): sold[jan] + backlog[jan] = demand[jan] (all demand either sold or backordered)
Constraint: Sold definition (lag): sold[t] + backlog[t] = demand[t] + backlog[t-1] (current demand plus prior backlog either sold or re-backordered)
Constraint: Inventory balance (init): inventory[jan] = initial_inventory + produce[jan] + outsource[jan] - sold[jan]
Constraint: Inventory balance (lag): inventory[t] = inventory[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t] - sold[t]
Constraint: Labor capacity: produce[t] * labor_per_unit <= regular_hours_per_worker * workforce[t] + overtime_hours[t]
Constraint: Overtime limit: overtime_hours[t] <= max_overtime_per_worker * workforce[t]
Constraint: Terminal inventory: inventory[jun] >= min_terminal_inventory
Constraint: Terminal backorder: backlog[jun] = 0

Title: Bill-of-Materials Production Planning
Keywords: BOM parameter
Description: A factory produces a set of finished products. Each finished product is assembled from components according to a Bill of Materials (BOM): producing one unit of product p requires a known quantity of each component c. Each component has a limited available supply. Each product has a known market demand cap (maximum units the market will absorb) and a profit per unit produced. Decide how many units of each product to produce to maximize total profit, subject to not exceeding component supply limits and market demand caps.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit from production, summed over all products weighted by units produced
Decision variables: produce[p]: units of product p to produce (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: profit[p]: profit per unit of product p produced; max_demand[p]: maximum units of product p that the market will absorb; bom[c,p]: units of component c required to produce one unit of product p; component_supply[c]: total available supply of component c
Constraint: Production of each product must not exceed that product's market demand cap
Constraint: For each component, the total component consumption across all products (according to BOM recipes) must not exceed the available component supply

examples.name: production_mix_typed_machines
examples.text:
Title: Multi-Stage Production Mix with Typed Machine Sets
Keywords: balance constraint, domain filter, filter_column subset, sparse filter
Description: A factory produces three products (I, II, III). Each product must pass through two sequential processing stages: stage A and stage B. Two A-type machines (A1, A2) and three B-type machines (B1, B2, B3) are available. Processing times differ by machine-product pair; not all machine-product combinations are feasible (sparse). Each unit of a product must be processed on exactly one A-machine and exactly one B-machine. Maximize total profit = revenue - raw material cost - machine operating cost.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit: revenue from all products minus raw material costs and machine operating costs (cost_per_hour * processing_time * units processed)
Decision variables: process_A[mA, p]: units of product p processed on A-machine mA (continuous, non-negative; only feasible machine-product pairs); process_B[mB, p]: units of product p processed on B-machine mB (continuous, non-negative; only feasible machine-product pairs); produce[p]: total units of product p produced (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: unit_price[p]: selling price per unit of product p; raw_material_cost[p]: raw material cost per unit of product p; effective_hours_A[mA]: available processing hours on A-machine mA; effective_hours_B[mB]: available processing hours on B-machine mB; cost_per_hour_A[mA]: processing cost per hour on A-machine mA; cost_per_hour_B[mB]: processing cost per hour on B-machine mB; processing_time_A[mA, p]: hours to process one unit of p on A-machine mA (sparse: not all pairs defined); processing_time_B[mB, p]: hours to process one unit of p on B-machine mB (sparse: not all pairs defined)
Constraint: A-stage balance: total units processed on all A-machines for product p equals total units produced of p
Constraint: B-stage balance: total units processed on all B-machines for product p equals total units produced of p
Constraint: A-machine capacity: total processing time on each A-machine does not exceed effective available hours
Constraint: B-machine capacity: total processing time on each B-machine does not exceed effective available hours

Title: Bill-of-Materials Production Planning with Alternative BOMs
Keywords: BOM parameter
Description: A factory produces a set of finished products. Each finished product can be assembled using one or more alternative Bill of Materials (BOM) configurations. Producing one unit of product p using BOM b requires a known quantity of each component c as specified by that BOM. Different BOMs for the same product may use different components or different quantities, for example substituting one raw material for another. Each component has a limited available supply shared across all products and BOMs. Each product has a known market demand cap (maximum total units the market will absorb, regardless of which BOM is used). Each product has a per-unit profit that does not depend on which BOM is used. Decide how many units of each product to produce under each BOM to maximize total profit, subject to not exceeding component supply limits and market demand caps.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit from production, summed over all products and recipes weighted by units produced
Decision variables: produce[p,b]: units of product p produced using BOM recipe b (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: profit[p]: profit per unit of product p produced (independent of recipe); max_demand[p]: maximum total units of product p that the market will absorb across all recipes; bom[c,p,b]: units of component c required to produce one unit of product p using recipe b; component_supply[c]: total available supply of component c
Constraint: For each product, the total units produced across all recipes must not exceed that product's market demand cap
Constraint: For each component, the total component consumption across all products and recipes (according to BOM quantities) must not exceed the available component supply

examples.text:
Title: Production Line Activation MIP: Maximize Profit with Fixed Setup Costs
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A factory can produce 3 products (A1, A2, A3) in a month (22 working days). Each product has a maximum market demand, net profit margin, daily production quota, a fixed activation cost if the production line is started, and a minimum batch size if activated. Decide whether to activate each product's line and how much to produce to maximize total profit (revenue minus production cost minus activation cost).
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit = sum over products of (margin[p] * produce[p] - activation_cost[p] * activate[p])
Decision variables: produce[p]: units of product p produced (continuous, non-negative); activate[p]: 1 if product p line is activated, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: margin[p]: net profit per unit produced (selling price - production cost); quota[p]: max units per day if all 22 days devoted to product p; activation_cost[p]: fixed cost to activate product p's line; min_batch[p]: minimum units if product p is activated; max_demand[p]: maximum market demand for product p; big_m[p]: min(22*quota[p], max_demand[p]) used as big-M coefficient; days_per_unit[p]: 1/quota[p], days consumed per unit of product p produced
Constraint: Working day limit: sum over products of produce[p] * days_per_unit[p] <= 22 (total production days cannot exceed 22)
Constraint: Production capacity: if activated, max produce = min(22*quota, max_demand); if not activated, produce = 0
Constraint: Minimum batch: if activated, produce >= min_batch
Constraint: Demand cap: produce[p] <= max_demand[p]

examples.text:
Title: Furniture Factory Single-Period Production Mix
Keywords: integer variable
Description: A furniture factory produces chairs, tables, and shelves. Each product type requires a certain number of labor-hours and board-feet of wood per unit. The factory has a fixed supply of labor hours and wood for the period. Products can only be produced in whole units — no fractional quantities. Each product type has a maximum production capacity due to machine constraints. Each product type earns a revenue per unit produced and incurs a variable per unit production cost. Determine how many units of each product type to produce to maximize total profit.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total profit across all products, where profit is total revenue minus total variable production cost
Decision variables: produce[p]: integer number of units of product p to produce
Parameters: revenue_per_unit[p]: revenue earned per unit of product p sold; production_cost[p]: variable cost per unit of product p produced; labor_hours[p]: labor-hours required to produce one unit of product p; wood_board_feet[p]: board-feet of wood required to produce one unit of product p; max_capacity[p]: maximum number of units of product p that can be produced in the period; labor_capacity: total labor-hours available for the period; wood_capacity: total board-feet of wood available for the period
Constraint: Total labor-hours consumed across all products cannot exceed the factory's fixed labor capacity for the period
Constraint: Total board-feet of wood consumed across all products cannot exceed the factory's fixed wood supply for the period
Constraint: Production of each product type cannot exceed its maximum machine capacity for the period

examples.name: project_scheduling
examples.text:
Title: Project Scheduling LP: Minimize Duration and Machine Rental Cost
Keywords: minimax objective, no sets, precedence constraint
Description: A project has 7 activities (A through G) with fixed durations: A=4, B=3, C=5, D=2, E=10, F=10, G=1 days. Precedence constraints: A must finish before G and D start; E and G must finish before F starts; D and F must finish before C starts; F must finish before B starts. A machine is rented from the start of activity A until the end of activity B (duration = start_B + 3 - start_A days). Total project duration T = max finish time across all activities. Minimize cost = 1000*T + 5000*machine_days.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = 1000 * T + 5000 * machine_days
Decision variables: t_A, t_B, t_C, t_D, t_E, t_F, t_G: start times of each activity (scalar continuous, non-negative); T: total project duration (scalar continuous, non-negative); machine_days: days the machine is rented (scalar continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Precedence A->G: t_G >= t_A + 4
Constraint: Precedence A->D: t_D >= t_A + 4
Constraint: Precedence E->F: t_F >= t_E + 10
Constraint: Precedence G->F: t_F >= t_G + 1
Constraint: Precedence D->C: t_C >= t_D + 2
Constraint: Precedence F->C: t_C >= t_F + 10
Constraint: Precedence F->B: t_B >= t_F + 10
Constraint: T >= finish time of each activity (7 constraints)
Constraint: machine_days = t_B + 3 - t_A

problem.title: Project Scheduling LP: Minimize Duration and Machine Rental Cost
problem.description: A project has 7 activities (A through G) with fixed durations: A=4, B=3, C=5, D=2, E=10, F=10, G=1 days. Precedence constraints: A must finish before G and D start; E and G must finish before F starts; D and F must finish before C starts; F must finish before B starts. A machine is rented from the start of activity A until the end of activity B (duration = start_B + 3 - start_A days). Total project duration T = max finish time across all activities. Minimize cost = 1000*T + 5000*machine_days.
problem.objective_description: Total cost = 1000 * T + 5000 * machine_days

constraints.description: Precedence A->G: t_G >= t_A + 4
Precedence A->D: t_D >= t_A + 4
Precedence E->F: t_F >= t_E + 10
Precedence G->F: t_F >= t_G + 1
Precedence D->C: t_C >= t_D + 2
Precedence F->C: t_C >= t_F + 10
Precedence F->B: t_B >= t_F + 10
T >= finish time of each activity (7 constraints)
machine_days = t_B + 3 - t_A

decision_variables: t_A, t_B, t_C, t_D, t_E, t_F, t_G: start times of each activity (scalar continuous, non-negative)
T: total project duration (scalar continuous, non-negative)
machine_days: days the machine is rented (scalar continuous, non-negative)
problem.additional_notes: All constraints use domain=[] (scalar). No sets or parameters needed; all data is hardcoded as constants. Optimal: t_A=0, t_E=0, t_G=4, t_D=4, t_F=14, t_C=24, t_B=24, T=27, machine_days=27. Wait - let me recheck. t_F >= t_G+1=5 and t_F >= t_E+10=10, so t_F=10 if t_E=0 and t_G=4. Then t_B>=t_F+10=20, t_C>=max(t_D+2,t_F+10)=max(6,20)=20. So T>=max(t_A+4,t_B+3,t_C+5,t_D+2,t_E+10,t_F+10,t_G+1)=max(4,23,25,6,10,20,5)=25. machine_days=t_B+3-t_A=20+3-0=23. Obj=1000*25+5000*23=25000+115000=140000. Actually expected is 115000: T=25, machine=18. Recheck: if t_A=5, t_E=0, t_G=9, t_D=9, t_F=10, t_B=20, T=25 (from t_B+3=23... no). Let me re-examine. If t_A can start later, t_E=0, t_F=10, t_B=20, T=max(t_B+3,t_C+5,...)=23 if t_C=18. machine_days=t_B+3-t_A=23-t_A. To minimize: push t_A as late as possible. t_A needs t_G=t_A+4 and t_F>=t_G+1=t_A+5, but t_F=10 is fixed by E path. So t_A+5<=10 => t_A<=5. With t_A=5: t_G=9, t_F>=max(10,10)=10, t_D=9, t_C>=max(11,20)=20, t_B>=20, T=max(9,23,25,11,10,20,10)=25. machine_days=23-5=18. Obj=25000+90000=115000. Correct!

Title: 24-Hour Restaurant Shift Scheduling
Keywords: integer variable, sparse filter
Description: A restaurant operates around the clock. In each 4-hour block of the day the minimum number of waiters required is given. Title: Retail Shelf Space Allocation

Description: A retailer allocates shelf space (facings) to products across store sections. A binary carry variable determines if a product is stocked. Constraint: Min facing: total facings per product >= min_facing if product is carried

Constraint: Max products: at most max_products products can be carried

Title: Preventive Machine Maintenance Scheduling
Keywords: binary variable
Description: A factory has five machines that require periodic preventive maintenance over an eight-period planning horizon. Each machine must receive at least a minimum number of maintenance sessions and at most a maximum number during the horizon (reflecting reliability requirements and maintenance contracts). Constraint: Each machine must receive at least min_maintenance maintenance sessions over the planning horizon
Constraint: Each machine must receive at most max_maintenance maintenance sessions over the planning horizon
Constraint: The total number of machines maintained in any period must not exceed the workshop capacity

Title: Multi-Period Workforce Adjustment Planning
Keywords: init constraint, integer variable, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturing company must plan its workforce size over six quarterly periods. In each period, the company can hire additional workers or lay off existing ones. Workforce adjustments carry transition costs: a fixed cost per new hire and a fixed cost per layoff. Workers also generate a recurring labor cost each period. The company must maintain a workforce level that meets the forecast demand in every period without exceeding a maximum headcount. The workforce in each period equals the previous period's workforce plus new hires minus layoffs. Starting workforce is given by a policy parameter.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost of hiring, firing, and labor across all periods
Decision variables: workforce[t]: number of workers employed in period t (non-negative integer); hire[t]: number of new workers hired at the start of period t (non-negative integer); fire[t]: number of workers laid off at the start of period t (non-negative integer)
Parameters: required_workers[t]: minimum workforce needed in period t; hire_cost[t]: cost per worker hired in period t; fire_cost[t]: cost per worker laid off in period t; labor_cost[t]: cost per worker employed in period t; initial_workforce: number of workers at the start of the planning horizon; max_workers: maximum allowed workforce at any time
Constraint: In the first period, workforce equals initial workforce plus hires minus fires
Constraint: In each subsequent period, workforce equals previous period workforce plus hires minus fires
Constraint: Workforce in each period must meet or exceed the required staffing level
Constraint: Workforce in each period must not exceed the maximum allowed headcount

examples.text:
Title: Seasonal Production Planning with Own and Rented Warehouse Storage
Keywords: balance constraint, init constraint, step cost, temporal lag
Description: A manufacturer plans production of two products (I and II) over 6 months (July through December) to minimize total production and storage cost. Monthly demand is low in Jul-Sep and high in Oct-Dec. Combined production capacity is 120,000 units/month. Product I requires 0.2 m3/unit volume and costs 4.5 yuan/unit to produce. Product II requires 0.4 m3/unit and costs 7 yuan/unit. Storage: the company owns a warehouse of 15,000 m3 (cost 1 yuan/m3/month); extra space can be rented at 1.5 yuan/m3/month. Initial inventory is zero.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = prod_cost[p,m]*produce[p,m] + 1*own_vol[m] + 1.5*ext_vol[m], summed over all products and months
Decision variables: produce[p,m]: units of product p produced in month m (continuous, non-negative); inv[p,m]: units of product p in inventory at end of month m (continuous, non-negative); own_vol[m]: m3 stored in own warehouse at end of month m (continuous, non-negative); ext_vol[m]: m3 stored in rented extra warehouse at end of month m (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,m]: units of product p demanded in month m; prod_cost[p,m]: production cost per unit of product p in month m; vol[p]: volume per unit of product p (m3/unit)
Constraint: Inventory balance init (July): inv[p,Jul] = produce[p,Jul] - demand[p,Jul], with zero initial inventory
Constraint: Inventory balance (Aug-Dec): inv[p,m] = inv[p,m-1] + produce[p,m] - demand[p,m]
Constraint: Monthly production capacity: sum over products of produce[p,m] <= 120000
Constraint: Warehouse volume: total volume stored = own_vol[m] + ext_vol[m]
Constraint: Own warehouse capacity: own_vol[m] <= 15000

Title: Emergency Response Station Siting
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable
Description: A city emergency management agency must site a minimum number of emergency response stations to ensure every residential neighborhood is covered. There are several candidate locations for new stations. For each candidate location it is known in advance which neighborhoods it can reach within the required response time — this is given as a binary coverage matrix. A neighborhood is considered covered if at least one open station can reach it within the time limit. Choose the minimum number of stations to open (and which locations to use) such that every neighborhood has at least one station covering it.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total number of emergency response stations opened across all candidate locations
Decision variables: open_station[c]: 1 if a station is opened at candidate location c, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: covers[c,n]: 1 if candidate location c can cover neighborhood n within the required response time, 0 otherwise
Constraint: For each neighborhood, the sum of coverage indicators over all open stations must be at least 1 (every neighborhood must be covered by at least one station)

examples.name: single_source
examples.text:
Title: Single-Source Supplier Selection
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter
Description: A manufacturer must source raw materials for a set of factories from a set of approved suppliers. Due to a quality-control policy, each factory must source all of its material from exactly one supplier — split orders across multiple suppliers are not allowed. Each supplier has a total supply capacity that limits the total quantity it can ship to all factories. The unit sourcing cost from each supplier to each factory is known. Choose which supplier serves each factory and how much is shipped to minimize total sourcing cost, while satisfying all factory demands, respecting supplier capacities, and enforcing the single-source assignment rule.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total sourcing cost = sum of per-unit costs times quantities shipped, over all supplier-factory pairs
Decision variables: source_from[s,f]: 1 if factory f is assigned to source from supplier s, 0 otherwise (binary); flow[s,f]: quantity of material shipped from supplier s to factory f (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: unit_cost[s,f]: per-unit sourcing cost from supplier s to factory f; demand[f]: total material required by factory f; supply_capacity[s]: maximum total quantity supplier s can ship to all factories
Constraint: Each factory must be assigned to exactly one supplier (single-source constraint)
Constraint: For each factory, total material received from all suppliers must exactly equal the factory's demand
Constraint: For each supplier, total quantity shipped to all factories must not exceed the supplier's capacity
Constraint: For each supplier-factory pair, quantity shipped cannot exceed the factory's demand times whether that supplier is assigned to that factory (big-M flow linking: no flow from an unassigned supplier)

examples.text:
Title: Stochastic Newsvendor — Multi-Product
Keywords: deviation variables, scenario weighted sum, two-stage stochastic
Description: A retailer orders multiple products before the selling season. Demand for each product is uncertain with 3 equally likely scenarios. For each scenario the retailer sells min(order, demand) and salvages leftover units. Maximize expected profit (revenue from sales plus salvage value minus ordering cost).
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Expected profit = E[sell_price * sell + salvage_price * leftover - unit_cost * order]
Decision variables: order[Products]: first-stage order quantity before demand is known (continuous, non-negative); sell[Products,Scenarios]: units sold in scenario s (continuous, non-negative); leftover[Products,Scenarios]: unsold units in scenario s (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: unit_cost[Products]: ordering cost per unit; sell_price[Products]: revenue per unit sold; salvage_price[Products]: salvage value per unsold unit; demand[Products,Scenarios]: demand in each scenario; probability[Scenarios]: scenario probability
Constraint: sell_limit_order: units sold cannot exceed the order quantity
Constraint: sell_limit_demand: units sold cannot exceed the realised demand
Constraint: inventory_balance: sell + leftover = order (balance split variables to order quantity)

Constraint: Sell limit (stock): cannot sell more than received from all suppliers

Constraint: Inventory balance: sell + leftover = total received

Title: 3-Year Investment LP: Maximize Wealth with Two Investment Options
Keywords: balance constraint, no sets, temporal lag
Description: An investor has 100,000 yuan. Option 1: 1-year term, returns 1.7x (profit 0.7 per yuan). Option 2: 2-year term (must be multiples of 2 years), returns 3x (profit 2 per yuan). Maximize total wealth at end of year 3 by choosing when and how much to invest each year.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Final wealth = 1.7 * opt1_yr3, where opt1_yr3 is the year-3 option-1 investment amount
Decision variables: opt1_yr1: yuan invested in option 1 at year 1 (continuous, >=0); opt2_yr1: yuan invested in option 2 at year 1 (continuous, >=0); opt1_yr2: yuan invested in option 1 at year 2 (continuous, >=0); opt1_yr3: yuan invested in option 1 at year 3 (continuous, >=0)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Year 1 budget: opt1_yr1 + opt2_yr1 = 100000
Constraint: Year 2 budget: opt1_yr2 = 1.7 * opt1_yr1 (reinvest all year-1 option-1 returns)
Constraint: Year 3 budget: opt1_yr3 = 3 * opt2_yr1 + 1.7 * opt1_yr2 (reinvest all year-2 returns)

Title: Toy Manufacturing MIP: Maximize Profit with Logical Production Rules
Keywords: big-M linking, implication constraint, mutual exclusion, no sets
Description: Factory makes robots ($15 profit), model cars ($8), building blocks ($12), dolls ($5). Resources: 1200 plastic units, 800 electronics units. Usage per unit: robot(30p,8e), car(10p,5e), block(20p,3e), doll(15p,2e). Rules: if robots produced → no dolls; if cars produced → blocks must also be produced; dolls ≤ cars count. Maximize profit.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Profit = 15*x_robots + 8*x_cars + 12*x_blocks + 5*x_dolls
Decision variables: x_robots, x_cars, x_blocks, x_dolls: continuous production amounts (>=0); z_robots, z_cars: binary indicators (1 if that product is manufactured)
Parameters: 
Constraint: Plastic: 30*robots + 10*cars + 20*blocks + 15*dolls <= 1200
Constraint: Electronics: 8*robots + 5*cars + 3*blocks + 2*dolls <= 800
Constraint: Dolls <= cars: x_dolls <= x_cars
Constraint: Robots indicator: x_robots <= 10000 * z_robots
Constraint: If robots, no dolls: x_dolls <= 10000 * (1 - z_robots)
Constraint: Cars indicator: x_cars <= 10000 * z_cars
Constraint: If cars, must produce blocks: x_blocks >= z_cars

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Regional Distribution
Keywords: domain filter
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Due to geographic constraints, only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes, and the same set of routes is used for all products and periods. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost that does not vary by product or period. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Determine how much of each product to ship along each available route in each period to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period

examples.text:
Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Route-Level and Site-Level Flow Allocation
Keywords: domain filter, duplicate set
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Additionally, certain routes are subject to flow allocation constraints: the total flow on a given route from a warehouse (summed over products) must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow on another route from the same warehouse. Similarly, certain warehouse pairs are subject to site-level flow allocation constraints: the total flow through one warehouse (summed over all routes, products, and in each period) must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow through another warehouse in that period. Determine how much of each product to ship along each valid route in each period to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies, while satisfying all route-level and site-level flow allocation requirements, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met; min_route_share_pct[w,c1,c2]: minimum fraction such that total flow from warehouse w to customer c1 must be at least this fraction of total flow from warehouse w to customer c2 (sparse: defined only for constrained route pairs); min_site_share_pct[w1,w2]: minimum fraction such that total flow through warehouse w1 must be at least this fraction of total flow through warehouse w2 per period (sparse: defined only for constrained warehouse pairs)
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period
Constraint: For each (warehouse, primary-customer, reference-customer, period) tuple listed in the route allocation table, the total flow (summed over products) shipped from the warehouse to the primary customer must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow shipped from the same warehouse to the reference customer in that period; trivially satisfied (0 >= 0) for all other combinations
Constraint: For each (warehouse1, warehouse2, period) tuple listed in the site allocation table, the total flow (summed over all customers and products) shipped out of warehouse1 must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow shipped out of warehouse2 in that period; trivially satisfied for all other combinations

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Flow Capacity and Route Activation
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, domain filter, sparse filter
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. Each route also has a maximum throughput capacity per product per period — the amount of a given product that can be shipped on a given route in a given period is bounded. A route may only carry shipments in a period if it is explicitly activated for that period; activating a route is a binary decision. Due to operational constraints, at most six routes may be simultaneously active in any given period. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Determine which routes to activate each period and how much of each product to ship along each active route to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies or route throughput capacities, while keeping active routes per period at most six, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes); active_route[w,c,t]: 1 if the route from warehouse w to customer c is activated in period t, 0 otherwise (binary, defined only for valid routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met; route_capacity[w,c,p]: maximum units of product p that can be shipped from warehouse w to customer c in any single period (defined only for valid routes)
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period
Constraint: For each valid route, product, and period, the amount shipped cannot exceed the route's throughput capacity for that product multiplied by whether the route is active in that period (big-M linking constraint)
Constraint: For each period, the total number of active routes across all valid warehouse-customer pairs must not exceed six

examples.text:
Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Truck Type Selection
Keywords: domain filter, integer variable, sparse filter
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Due to geographic constraints, only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. In addition, all shipments must be transported in discrete trucks. Three truck types are available (small, medium, large), each with a different cargo capacity (maximum total units carried per trip) and a fixed dispatch cost charged per truck used, regardless of how full it is. For each warehouse-customer route in each period, the company chooses how many trucks of each type to dispatch. The total cargo capacity of dispatched trucks on a route must cover the total volume of all products shipped on that route in that period. Each warehouse has a known supply of each product each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Minimize total cost: per-unit shipping costs across all products and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs for all trucks used.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: per-unit shipping costs summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs summed over all valid routes, truck types, and periods
Decision variables: ship[i,j,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse i to customer j in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid routes); trucks[i,j,k,t]: number of trucks of type k dispatched from warehouse i to customer j in period t (integer, non-negative, defined only for valid routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[i,j]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse i to customer j, shared across all products and periods (defined only for valid routes); supply[i,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse i in period t; demand[j,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer j in period t, which must be exactly met; truck_size[k]: cargo capacity in units for one truck of type k (maximum total units that one truck can carry per trip); truck_fixed_cost[k]: fixed dispatch cost per truck of type k used on any route in any period
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's available supply
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount received from all warehouses via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand
Constraint: For each valid route and period, the total volume shipped across all products must not exceed the combined cargo capacity of all trucks dispatched on that route in that period

problem.title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Truck Type Selection
problem.description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Due to geographic constraints, only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. In addition, all shipments must be transported in discrete trucks. Three truck types are available (small, medium, large), each with a different cargo capacity (maximum total units carried per trip) and a fixed dispatch cost charged per truck used, regardless of how full it is. For each warehouse-customer route in each period, the company chooses how many trucks of each type to dispatch. The total cargo capacity of dispatched trucks on a route must cover the total volume of all products shipped on that route in that period. Each warehouse has a known supply of each product each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Minimize total cost: per-unit shipping costs across all products and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs for all trucks used.
problem.objective_description: Total cost: per-unit shipping costs summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs summed over all valid routes, truck types, and periods

constraints.description: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's available supply
For each customer, product, and period, the total amount received from all warehouses via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand
For each valid route and period, the total volume shipped across all products must not exceed the combined cargo capacity of all trucks dispatched on that route in that period

decision_variables: ship[i,j,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse i to customer j in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid routes)
trucks[i,j,k,t]: number of trucks of type k dispatched from warehouse i to customer j in period t (integer, non-negative, defined only for valid routes)
parameters: transport_cost[i,j]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse i to customer j, shared across all products and periods (defined only for valid routes)
supply[i,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse i in period t
demand[j,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer j in period t, which must be exactly met
truck_size[k]: cargo capacity in units for one truck of type k (maximum total units that one truck can carry per trip)
truck_fixed_cost[k]: fixed dispatch cost per truck of type k used on any route in any period
problem.additional_notes: The truck_capacity_cover constraint links continuous shipment volumes to integer truck counts: the sum of all products shipped on a route in a period cannot exceed the total cargo capacity of dispatched trucks. Using larger trucks is more cost-efficient per unit of capacity but incurs a higher fixed charge, creating a trade-off between truck type and shipment volume. Multiple truck types may be combined on the same route and period.

Title: Two-Echelon Transshipment MIP with Fixed Station Costs
Keywords: big-M linking, flow conservation
Description: Minimize cost to ship containers from 2 production sites (S1 supply=100, S2 supply=150) through 2 intermediate stations (K1 cap=100 fixed=10, K2 cap=100 fixed=15) to 2 demand points (D1=80, D2=120). Per-unit shipping costs: site-to-station c1[S1,K1]=2, c1[S1,K2]=3, c1[S2,K1]=4, c1[S2,K2]=1; station-to-demand c2[K1,D1]=3, c2[K1,D2]=2, c2[K2,D1]=1, c2[K2,D2]=4. A station incurs its fixed cost only if it handles any flow (binary open variable linked to capacity).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum(c1*flow1) + sum(c2*flow2) + sum(fixed_cost*open)
Decision variables: flow1[s,k]: continuous, units shipped from site s to station k (lb=0); flow2[k,d]: continuous, units shipped from station k to demand d (lb=0); open[k]: binary, 1 if station k is used
Parameters: supply[s]: production capacity of site s; demand_req[d]: demand at demand point d; capacity[k]: throughput capacity of station k; fixed_cost[k]: fixed operating cost if station k is opened; cost1[s,k]: per-unit shipping cost from site s to station k; cost2[k,d]: per-unit shipping cost from station k to demand d
Constraint: Supply limit: total flow from site s to all stations <= supply[s]
Constraint: Demand satisfaction: total flow to demand d from all stations >= demand[d]
Constraint: Flow conservation at station k: inflow from sites = outflow to demands
Constraint: Station capacity: total inflow to station k <= capacity[k] * open[k]
