examples.text:
Title: Traveling Salesman Problem with MTZ Subtour Elimination
Keywords: MTZ subtour elimination, binary variable, duplicate set, exclude diagonal, filter_column subset, set size expression
Description: A salesman must visit 7 cities exactly once and return to the starting city (city 1, the depot). The distance between every pair of cities is given in a symmetric matrix stored as directed arcs (both directions included). Minimize total travel distance. The model uses a depot/customer structure: city 1 is the depot and cities 2-7 are customers. MTZ subtour elimination constraints prevent disconnected sub-tours among customer nodes.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total travel distance of the complete tour starting and ending at the depot
Decision variables: x[c1, c2]: binary arc variable, 1 if the salesman travels directly from city c1 to city c2 (exclude diagonal: no self-loops); u[c]: integer position variable for non-depot customers, used in MTZ subtour elimination (lb=1, ub=|Customers|)
Parameters: distance[c1, c2]: travel distance from city c1 to city c2 (symmetric, stored as directed arcs, no diagonal)
Constraint: Each city is departed exactly once: for each city c, sum over all j of x[c,j] = 1
Constraint: Each city is entered exactly once: for each city c, sum over all i of x[i,c] = 1
Constraint: MTZ subtour elimination: for customer pairs (c1,c2) with c1 != c2, u[c1] - u[c2] + n*x[c1,c2] <= n-1 where n = |Cities|

examples.name: unit_commitment
examples.text:
Title: Unit Commitment Problem
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, init constraint, temporal lag
Description: A power system operator schedules three generators over 8 hours. Each generator has minimum and maximum output limits, a fuel cost per MWh, and a startup cost when brought online. A binary commit variable determines if a generator is online each hour. Generation is only possible when committed (big-M linking). A binary startup variable captures when a generator transitions from off to on. Power balance must be met each hour. Minimize total fuel plus startup costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of fuel costs (fuel_cost[g]*generate[g,t]) plus startup costs (startup_cost[g]*startup[g,t]) over all generators and hours
Decision variables: commit[g,t]: 1 if generator g is online in hour t (binary); generate[g,t]: MW output of generator g in hour t (continuous, non-negative); startup[g,t]: 1 if generator g starts up at hour t (binary)
Parameters: fuel_cost[g]: cost per MWh for generator g; startup_cost[g]: fixed cost when generator g starts up; min_output[g]: minimum MW output when generator g is online; max_output[g]: maximum MW output when generator g is online; demand[t]: MW demand in hour t
Constraint: Power balance: total generation equals demand each hour
Constraint: Minimum generation: when committed, generate at least min_output (big-M lower bound)
Constraint: Maximum generation: when committed, generate at most max_output (big-M upper bound)
Constraint: Startup link init: startup[g,h1] >= commit[g,h1] (first period, no previous state)
Constraint: Startup link: startup[g,t] >= commit[g,t] - commit[g,t-1] for subsequent periods (temporal lag)

examples.text:
Title: Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) with MTZ Subtour Elimination
Keywords: MTZ subtour elimination, binary variable, duplicate set, exclude diagonal, init constraint, integer variable, set size expression, upper bound set
Description: A delivery company must route a fleet of vehicles from a central depot to serve a set of customers, then return to the depot. Each customer has a known demand. Each vehicle has a fixed load capacity — the total demand of all customers on a vehicle's route cannot exceed its capacity. The travel distance (cost) between every pair of locations (depot and customers) is known. Each customer must be visited exactly once by exactly one vehicle. Subtour elimination is enforced via Miller-Tucker-Zemlin (MTZ) constraints using integer position variables. Find the set of routes — one per vehicle — that minimizes total travel distance while serving all customers within vehicle capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total travel distance across all activated arcs (vehicle routes), summed over all vehicle-arc combinations
Decision variables: y[l1,l2,v]: 1 if vehicle v travels directly from location l1 to location l2, 0 otherwise (binary, self-loops excluded); u[c,v]: visit position of customer c in vehicle v's route, used for MTZ subtour elimination (integer, lower bound 1)
Parameters: distance[l1,l2]: travel distance from location l1 to location l2; demand[c]: units of goods required by customer c; vehicle_capacity: maximum load each vehicle can carry (uniform across all vehicles)
Constraint: Each customer must be visited exactly once across all vehicles and all incoming arcs
Constraint: For each location and vehicle, the number of arcs entering that location equals the number leaving (flow conservation)
Constraint: Each vehicle departs the depot at most once (depot departure)
Constraint: Each vehicle returns to the depot at most once (depot return)
Constraint: For each vehicle, the total demand of all customers visited must not exceed the vehicle's load capacity
Constraint: MTZ subtour elimination: for each pair of distinct customers and each vehicle, if vehicle v travels directly from customer c1 to c2, then the visit position of c2 must be at least one more than c1's position, preventing subtours

Title: Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW)
Keywords: MTZ subtour elimination, big-M linking, binary variable, duplicate set, exclude diagonal, init constraint, integer variable, set size expression, upper bound set
Description: A depot must deliver goods to several customers using a fleet of vehicles. Each vehicle starts from the depot, visits a subset of customers, and returns to the depot. Each customer has a demand that must be satisfied, a vehicle capacity must not be exceeded, and each customer must be visited within a specified time window (earliest and latest arrival time). Travel times are known between every pair of locations. Service at each customer takes a fixed duration. The objective is to minimize total travel distance.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total travel distance across all vehicle arcs used
Decision variables: y[l1,l2,v]: 1 if vehicle v travels directly from location l1 to location l2, else 0 (binary, exclude self-loops); u[c,v]: position of customer c in vehicle v's route (integer, used for MTZ subtour elimination); arrive[c,v]: arrival time of vehicle v at customer c (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: distance[l1,l2]: travel distance from location l1 to location l2; travel_time[l1,l2]: travel time from location l1 to location l2; demand[c]: delivery demand at customer c; service_time[c]: time spent servicing customer c; tw_lb[c]: earliest acceptable arrival time at customer c; tw_ub[c]: latest acceptable arrival time at customer c; vehicle_capacity: maximum load per vehicle; big_m: large constant for time-window big-M linking constraints
Constraint: Each customer is visited exactly once across all vehicles
Constraint: Flow conservation: arcs entering and leaving each location balance for each vehicle
Constraint: Each vehicle departs from the depot at most once
Constraint: Each vehicle returns to the depot at most once
Constraint: Vehicle capacity: total customer demand served by each vehicle must not exceed the vehicle capacity
Constraint: MTZ subtour elimination: position variables prevent sub-tours among customers
Constraint: Departure time from depot: arrival time at each customer visited from the depot is at least the depot-to-customer travel time (big-M linking)
Constraint: Time propagation: arrival time at the next customer accounts for service time and travel time at the current customer (big-M linking)
Constraint: Time window lower bound: each vehicle must arrive at a customer no earlier than the time window opens (enforced only when the customer is visited by that vehicle)
Constraint: Time window upper bound: each vehicle must arrive at a customer no later than the time window closes

Title: Bin Packing with Weight and Packaging Constraints
Keywords: big-M linking, binary variable, implication constraint, integer variable
Description: A company must pack five types of goods (A: 120 units/0.5t each; B: 90 units/1t each; C: 300 units/0.4t each; D: 90 units/0.6t each; E: 120 units/0.65t each) into containers. Each container holds at most 60 tons and must be loaded with at least 18 tons if used. Every used container must contain at least 12 units of good D. If any good A is loaded in a container, at least 1 unit of good C must also be in that container. Minimize the total number of containers used.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total number of containers used
Decision variables: x[i,k]: integer units of item type i in container k (non-negative integer); y[k]: binary, 1 if container k is used; z[k]: binary, 1 if container k contains any A items
Parameters: total_units[i]: total number of units of item type i to be packed; weight_per_unit[i]: weight in tons per unit of item type i
Constraint: All units of each item type must be packed: sum over containers of x[i,k] = total_units[i]
Constraint: Weight per used container cannot exceed 60 tons: sum_i(weight[i]*x[i,k]) <= 60*y[k]
Constraint: Each used container must hold at least 18 tons: sum_i(weight[i]*x[i,k]) >= 18*y[k]
Constraint: At least 12 units of D must be in each used container: x[D,k] >= 12*y[k]
Constraint: x[A,k] <= 120*z[k]: if A items exist in container k, z[k]=1
Constraint: x[C,k] >= z[k]: if z[k]=1 (container has A items), at least 1 C must be present

examples.name: workforce_scheduling
examples.text:
Title: Call Center Shift Scheduling
Keywords: binary variable
Description: A call center must staff a set of daily shifts using a pool of available employees. Each shift requires a minimum number of workers on duty to handle expected call volume. Each employee has a known cost associated with working each particular shift — reflecting overtime rates, preferences, or seniority differentials. No employee should work more than a specified maximum number of shifts per week to comply with labor regulations. Determine the minimum-cost schedule that assigns employees to shifts such that all minimum staffing requirements are met and no employee exceeds their weekly shift limit.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total labor cost across all employee-shift assignments where an employee is scheduled to work
Decision variables: work[e,s]: 1 if employee e is scheduled to work shift s, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: shift_cost[e,s]: cost of scheduling employee e to work shift s; min_coverage[s]: minimum number of employees required on shift s; max_shifts_per_employee: maximum number of shifts any employee may work per week
Constraint: For each shift, the total number of employees scheduled to work that shift must meet or exceed the minimum required staffing level
Constraint: For each employee, the total number of shifts they are scheduled to work must not exceed the maximum allowed shifts per week

examples.name: workforce_scheduling_fairness
examples.text:
Title: Workforce Scheduling with Fairness
Keywords: binary variable, deviation variables, sparse filter
Description: Schedule nurses across shifts and days with fairness. Coverage requirements must be met. Each nurse works at most one shift per day. Total shifts are counted; deviation from the target is penalized. Preferences are honored where possible. Minimize fairness penalty minus preference score.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total deviation from target shifts minus total preference score
Decision variables: work[n,s,d]: 1 if nurse n works shift s on day d (binary); total_shifts[n]: total shifts worked this week; excess[n]: shifts above target (continuous >= 0); deficit[n]: shifts below target (continuous >= 0)
Parameters: min_nurses[s,d]: minimum nurses needed per shift-day; max_per_day[n]: max shifts per nurse per day (all 1); preference[n,s,d]: preference score (sparse); target_shifts: target weekly shifts per nurse
Constraint: Minimum nurses per shift-day must be met
Constraint: Each nurse works at most one shift per day
Constraint: Total shifts for each nurse are counted
Constraint: Deviation variables capture excess/deficit from target

examples.name: workforce_upskilling
examples.text:
Title: Workforce Upskilling Planning
Keywords: binary variable, temporal lag
Description: A company trains workers over 4 quarters to acquire skills needed for upcoming projects. Once a worker gains a skill, they retain it. Training capacity limits how many workers can be trained per quarter. Skill supply (skilled workers) must meet demand each quarter. Minimize total training cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total training cost = sum over workers, skills, quarters of training_cost[w,sk] * train[w,sk,q]
Decision variables: train[Workers, Skills, Quarters]: 1 if worker w is trained in skill sk in quarter q (binary); skilled[Workers, Skills, Quarters]: 1 if worker w has skill sk by end of quarter q (binary)
Parameters: training_cost[Workers, Skills]: cost to train worker w in skill sk; skill_demand[Skills, Quarters]: number of workers needed with skill sk in quarter q; training_cap[Quarters]: maximum total trainings per quarter
Constraint: Skill accumulation: once skilled, a worker retains the skill (temporal lag - skills cannot decrease)
Constraint: Train to skill: training in a quarter makes the worker skilled that quarter
Constraint: Skill demand met: number of skilled workers per skill per quarter must meet demand
Constraint: Training capacity: total trainings per quarter cannot exceed capacity
